We formalize this view as Perturb-Select-Vote (PSV), a general procedure that generates perturbed predictors, selects high-performing members on a small validation set, and aggregates their predictions. This interpretation connects Neural Thickets to established inference-time methods, including sampling, self-consistency, and verifier-guided selection. A first-order analysis further shows that small weight perturbations act primarily through their induced logit shifts. We extend this analysis to vision, where logit PSV substantially improves performance under domain shift, including on Earth observation, while full-weight perturbations provide little additional benefit. Together, these results suggest that the gains attributed to nearby weight-space experts can instead be obtained through output diversity, selection, and voting. Logit PSV realizes these benefits with a fully frozen model, providing a simple, training-free alternative to full-weight perturbation ensembles across language and vision.

title: When Does Storage Complement Solar? Investment and Cost Recovery under Advanced Net Metering
abstract: We examine the joint PV and storage operational and investment decisions of a prosumer under net energy metering (NEM) and peak/off-peak tariffs. Legacy NEM compensates net exports at the retail rate over a netting period, typically under time-invariant pricing. To better reflect system costs, tariff features are being reconsidered, with many U.S. states adopting time-varying prices and export compensation below the retail price. We formulate the prosumer decision problem as a cost minimization problem with charge/discharge, PV investment, and storage investment decisions. We analytically derive the optimal decisions based on the tariff's membership in one of six regions that partition the tariff space. Using these solutions, we examine the relationship between PV and storage, identifying when they are complements or substitutes. Furthermore, we identify the relationship between private DER incentives and the distribution utility's (DU's) net cost of serving the prosumer. For both storage and PV, when investment costs are greater than the costs of serving the customer, there is no tariff where investment in PV and storage decrease non-adopter bills. Under the same conditions, complementarity between PV and storage decreases DU cost recovery for a given tariff. In a Massachusetts-based case study, we validate our theoretical findings by connecting tariff design features to DER interaction, the DU's net cost, and DER adoption in a stochastic, multi-prosumer, and multi-period setting.

title: Renormalization for Robust Memory without Synchronization
abstract: Local error correction can preserve classical information against noise, but protection under synchronized updates need not survive when sites evolve at independent random times. Establishing stability is particularly challenging when protection relies on the collective action of competing local rules. Here we develop a spacetime renormalization framework that reveals how independently acting local updates can collectively stabilize memory. We identify sufficient conditions under which the geometry of stable interfaces and suppression of defect propagation produce reliable erosion at large scales. Applying this framework, we prove stability of the asynchronous \textsf{R} squeezing code and introduce robust processes in two and three dimensions. In these systems, both encoded phases persist under sufficiently weak noise, even when the noise favors one phase. Our results provide a criterion for designing autonomous memories sustained by competing local stochastic dynamics.

title: Reconstructing hidden observables via quantum snapshot thermometry
abstract: Projective snapshots are a standard readout tool for quantum simulators, but they directly probe only observables that are diagonal in the measurement basis. We show how local equilibration and an independently calibrated equilibrium equation of state can reveal otherwise hidden conserved-density profiles. We demonstrate numerically that such ``quantum snapshot thermometry'' can recover energy fronts and a diffusion constant, distinguish spin transport from energy spreading, and reveal conserved-charge profiles invisible in the initial measurements. We also identify symmetry-imposed ambiguities in the readout and show how prior knowledge of the spatial structure can resolve them. Fixed-basis snapshot thermometry thus provides quantitative hydrodynamic information beyond transport exponents, bypassing additional measurement bases and quantum state tomography.

title: Micro-Edits: Computational Support for Fine-Scale Edits in Film
abstract: In film editing, every frame matters. While macro, content-level edits shape the high-level narrative of a film, small local edits often control timing and direct visual attention. For example, editors can adjust the precise timing of clips to control the length of a meaningful silence, or cut to shots that highlight a specific character's reactions to important moments. These small, detailed edits are slow and tedious to make in standard editing tools because users have to map high-level narrative goals to low-level frame-by-frame adjustments. At the same time, these fine-scale adjustments, which we call micro-edits, can be nuanced and expressive, with different choices serving different creative goals. In this work, we start by conducting a formative study with professional editors to understand the structure of micro-edits and how they are used. We then derive a mathematical formalization for this structure to develop tools that leverage AI and optimization to make exploring micro-edits simpler and more efficient for users. Finally, we validate our tools in multiple user studies and a wide range of video examples.

title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering
abstract: Differential privacy requires that algorithms be stable to the change of any record in their input, even to an extreme outlier. Private algorithms thus commonly introduce noise scaled to the worst-case possible influence of any single record. This work studies how to build differentially private algorithms that can effectively tailor their noise to the typical case rather than the worst case. We introduce the general \emph{propose-filter-release} (PFR) framework, which, by privately filtering its input, turns a mechanism that protects the addition or removal of a \emph{typical} record into one that is differentially private in the standard sense, on \emph{every} input. We show how to instantiate PFR with a novel filtering step to obtain a general meta-algorithm. Given only a concave friendliness score (which measures how typical a record is with respect to a dataset) and a release mechanism that is friendly-DP (that is, private conditioned on the changed record being typical of the remaining data), it guarantees differential privacy on sufficiently large datasets. The FriendlyCore [TCK+22] and Propose-Test-Release [DL09] algorithms can be viewed as instantiations of our general approach. We illustrate the generality of PFR by instantiating it for scalar statistics, principal subspace estimation with a dimension-independent sample size, the KL divergence of user histograms, the effective resistances in a resistor network, and treatment-rule selection.

title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
abstract: Data attribution methods for Language Models (LMs) are typically evaluated using downstream tasks like fact retrieval. However, existing evaluations vary multiple dataset properties simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate exactly why an attribution algorithm fails. To diagnose these failures, we explore the design space of LLM data attribution, with a primary focus on evaluation. We introduce the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) for fact tracing, in which we fine-tune LLMs on entirely fictitious knowledge, providing unambiguous ground truth for attribution. This synthetic setup allows us to systematically alter one dataset configuration at a time, such as document redundancy and lexical distractors. With this configurable evaluation, we demonstrate that redundancy and distractors consistently degrade attribution performance. Rather than proposing a new estimator, we examine two design choices that are underexplored: the loss used to compute gradients and how per-token attribution scores are aggregated into a document score. We find that the true causal evidence within a training document is highly localized, but standard methods dilute this evidence into noise by averaging attribution scores across the entire document. We find that replacing standard cross-entropy loss gradients with the negative log-odds gradients surfaces the critical tokens from other uninformative ones. We can then aggregate only the top token scores to improve ground truth recall by 35 to 72 percentage points across multiple baselines on our diagnostic benchmark. The negative log-odds correction also generalizes to FTRACE-TREX, improving counterfactual retraining performance for every method we test, by up to 4.9x.

title: The $δ$ Scuti instability strip and period-luminosity relation as seen by TESS and Gaia DR3
abstract: We present an asteroseismic survey of 1,526,218 A- and F-type stars in and around the $δ$ Scuti instability strip using TESS 10-minute cadence data, which resolve the full $δ$ Scuti pulsation spectra across nearly the entire sky. We derive homogeneous stellar parameters from Gaia DR3 parallaxes and archival photometry, with temperatures that agree with interferometry to within ~300 K. A Positive--Unlabelled classifier identifies 156,706 $δ$ Scuti pulsators, which on average rotate significantly faster than non-variable A-type stars. Within the instability strip in the $T_{eff}$--$\log L$ plane, the pulsator fraction peaks at 30% over the full sample and rises to 80% in the brightest magnitude bins. Detection sensitivity therefore accounts for much, but not all, of the apparent impurity of the strip. Our period--luminosity relation agrees with previous determinations, and we recast it as a scale-invariant period--density relation that connects directly to the pulsation constant. We find that the secondary ridge in these relations is probably a combination of several overtone modes. The $δ$ Scuti stars closest to the fundamental ridge have systematically lower rotational velocities and occupy a distinct region of the instability strip. Finally, a cross-match with a Gaia catalog of open clusters reveals a correlation between the mean pulsation frequency of $δ$ Scuti stars and cluster age, suggesting a new ensemble asteroseismic age indicator for young stellar populations.

title: Variational wavefunctions for ideal anyon gas: superfluid and skyrmion Hall crystal
abstract: The ground state of an ideal gas of anyons with statistical angle $θ\in(0,π)$ is a long-standing open problem, with renewed interest from the recent observations of fractional Chern insulators. In this work we construct variational wavefunctions that build in the exact anyon statistics and combine theory-guided composite-boson, composite-fermion and parton wavefunctions with neural-network correlations on the sphere. For spinless and SU(2) semions we confirm the paired anyon superfluid, well below the best crystal states. At $θ=π/3$ liquids and crystals are closer in energy for the spinless case. For $θ=π/3$ anyons with SU(3) flavor, we find two candidates. One is a skyrmion Hall crystal, in which the anyons form an integer quantum Hall state in the effective magnetic field from the spin texture. The other is a chiral color superconductor of six-anyon clusters, the color-flavor-locked pairing descendant of a holon metal with SU(3) color gauge symmetry and SU(3) flavor symmetry; its wavefunction is a hyperdeterminant rather than a product of parton determinants. Within our variational ansatz the color superconductor has better energy than both crystals and the color-flavor locked phases with U(1)$^2$ and Z$_3$ gauge groups. For twisted MoTe$_2$ this suggests that the reentrant integer quantum anomalous Hall phase is the skyrmion Hall crystal of the doped anyons, and that the observed superconductivity may be the color superconductor, which can undergo a transition to an $f+if$ BCS superconductor with a jump of the chiral central charge by 3.

title: Explain, Then Forget: Recommendation Unlearning under Asymmetric Access Constraint
abstract: Recommendation unlearning aims to remove the influence of specific historical interactions that should no longer affect future recommendations, such as noisy clicks or outdated user preferences. However, performing recommendation unlearning becomes much harder in modern Machine-Learning-as-a-Service (MLaaS) architectures, where the recommendation model is remotely hosted by a model provider (MP) and accessed by service operators (SO) only through APIs. In this setting, a service operator serves end users but cannot access or modify internal model parameters. As a result, existing unlearning methods are difficult to apply because they require access to model internals for retraining, fine-tuning, or other parameter updates. To address these challenges, we propose Causal Explanation-based Unlearning (CEU), a novel unlearning framework tailored for MLaaS environments. Instead of modifying internal model weights, CEU operates through a two-step output-level score intervention. First, it estimates how the forgotten interaction causally contributes to the current recommendation. Second, guided by this causal signal, the system removes the influence of the forgotten interaction by adjusting the final ranking scores of affected items. Because CEU leaves model parameters untouched, it naturally supports continuous unlearning requests while avoiding the error accumulation that can result from repeated parameter updates. Extensive experiments on three public datasets show that CEU achieves unlearning effectiveness comparable to full retraining while preserving recommendation utility and significantly reducing computational cost. The source code is available at: https://github.com/zhang-haichao/Explain-and-Forget.

title: Generalized supremum convolutions on the tensor product of unit intervals: t-conorms and triangle functions
abstract: The complete-lattice tensor product $\mathbb{E}=[0,1]\otimes[0,1]$ arises naturally in the algebra of truth values for type-2 fuzzy sets. For a monotone surjective map $S$ that is continuous on $[0,1[^2$ and a monotone map $T$ having $1$ as identity, we consider the generalized supremum convolution \[ (f\otimes_{_{S,T}}g)(x)=\sup_{S(u,v)=x}T(f(u),g(v)) \] on $\mathbb{E}$. Rather than assuming classical algebraic structures for $S$ and $T$ from the outset, we ask when they are forced by requiring the induced convolution itself to be a t-conorm. We prove that $\otimes_{_{S,T}}$ is a t-conorm on $\mathbb{E}$ if and only if $S$ is a continuous t-conorm and either $S=\max$ or $T$ is a right-continuous t-norm; in the exceptional case $S=\max$, the convolution is simply the pointwise maximum for every admissible $T$. The same convolution mechanism also yields an order-dual description of triangle functions on the space of distance distribution functions $Δ^+$. Using an order-reversing isomorphism between $Δ^+$ and a boundary variant of $\mathbb{E}$, we show that $τ_{_{T^*,L}}$ is a triangle function precisely when $L$ is a continuous t-conorm with no zero divisor and, unless $L=\max$, $T^*$ is a left-continuous t-conorm; moreover, when $L\neq\max$, continuity of $τ_{_{T^*,L}}$ is equivalent to continuity of $T^*$. This resolves the remaining $τ_{_{T^*,L}}$ part of the Schweizer--Sklar problem.

title: Adversarial Wronskians: A proof of the Kung--Traub conjecture
abstract: We prove the Kung--Traub conjecture: a deterministic stationary root-finding method without memory, using at most $n$ real scalar function or derivative evaluations per iteration, cannot have local order greater than $2^{n-1}$ on every real analytic function with a simple zero. For $n\geq2$, the bound is attained by the methods of Kung and Traub. The local estimate is required at every sufficiently close starting point, with constants that may depend on the function. Evaluation points and derivative orders may be chosen adaptively, and the rules for choosing them and processing the data are unrestricted. The proof uses a localisation property of polynomial Wronskians to obtain a lower bound at each fixed scale. A diagonal construction then gives one entire function, with derivative bounded above and below on the real line, for which every larger order fails. We also obtain a sharper bound when evaluations are made in prescribed groups, and prove the corresponding result for complex scalar evaluations. The results of this paper are also formally verified in Lean.

title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.

title: A small HER2 reader for routine H&E slides: real-world deployment
abstract: HER2 status decides who receives HER2-targeted therapy. Pathologists score HER2 protein by immunohistochemistry (IHC); equivocal IHC 2+ tumours, their hardest calls, wait for in situ hybridisation (ISH). We built a HER2 reader for routine H&E slides, owned end to end, as a baseline for pathologists. A 22M-parameter ViT-S/16 tile encoder was trained on public TCGA slides by self-supervision, distillation from H-optimus-0 and two rounds of JEPA refinement; five cross-validated attention-based slide classifiers average their probabilities; and an operating point is fixed on training data. Compared under one paired ten-seed protocol, readers on our encoder rank first of 7 on external validation from TCGA-BRCA to Yale-HER2 (AUC 0.812), level with readers on encoders 4 and 50 times larger. We also rebuilt PathBench's encoder benchmark on public cohorts; our replica reproduces its published order of reference encoders, and under it our encoder ranks first of 7 on TCGA-BRCA (0.689) and sits level with H-optimus-0 and Phikon on Yale-HER2 (0.897). On three external hospitals our deployed reader reaches AUC 0.82 on Yale-HER2 (about 0.81 with training slides balanced for tissue size), 0.75 on HEROHE and 0.63 on BCNB biopsies, and among HEROHE's 85 IHC 2+ cases it ranks ISH-amplified above non-amplified tumours at 0.76, best among our TCGA-trained readers. Per-laboratory score normalisation and a laboratory's own slides improve it further on a new site. Without a GPU our reader needs 5-6 s per slide. It serves as a research-use pre-read in a pathology platform, where it proposes a probability and a call beside IHC and helps prioritise ISH for equivocal cases. Weights, per-slide predictions and the data behind every figure are public at https://huggingface.co/cloudkites/her2-reader.

title: Learning from Expert-Corrected Misdiagnoses: A Self-Evolving Consultation Agent for Traditional Chinese Medicine after Failed Treatment
abstract: In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), treatment follows syndrome differentiation (bianzheng), the step that maps a patient's findings to a TCM syndrome. A misdiagnosed syndrome therefore leads directly to inappropriate treatment, and the error usually surfaces only after that treatment fails. The physician who sees the patient next must diagnose a condition already altered by the wrong therapy, identify the initial physician's error, and avoid continuing the failed therapeutic direction. We introduce TCM-MisDx, an interactive benchmark of 820 consultations after treatment failure built from three published monographs of TCM misdiagnosis cases. An agent gathers symptoms, tongue and pulse findings through the four diagnostic methods before reporting the current syndrome, the initial error, and a corrective treatment plan. We further present TCM-SEA, a self-evolving consultation agent that rewrites its own clinical skill document: failed consultations are compared with the expert physician's documented analysis, the agent proposes a minimal edit, and the edit is kept only if it passes an acceptance gate on held-in and held-out cases. The underlying language model is never updated. On the sealed test set, TCM-SEA raises the composite score from 61.8 to 65.5, syndrome accuracy from 53.9 to 57.2 and treatment-principle accuracy from 44.7 to 48.9, and lowers the therapeutic momentum rate, the fraction of corrective plans that keep the initial physician's failed direction, from 44.1 to 38.2. Learning from expert cases outperforms learning from outcome feedback alone, with the largest gains on the monograph of inappropriate-treatment cases. The two accepted edits are short, human-readable clinical checklists that physicians can audit directly.

title: Intervention-Conditioned Counterfactual Human Digital Twin Generator
abstract: Chronic diseases evolve through long, heterogeneous trajectories shaped by interacting mediators, confounders, and treatment histories. Estimating long-term patient trajectories under alternative interventions is essential for in silico clinical trial design. However, most existing models overlook irregular visit intervals and cross-mediator dependencies, both of which are crucial for reliable long-term longitudinal prediction. Moreover, these models typically focus on outcome prediction rather than generating complete patient-state trajectories. To address these challenges, we propose CHDT, an intervention-conditioned Human Digital Twin generator under standard identification assumptions for multimodal longitudinal trajectory estimation. Its main empirical advantage arises from explicit modeling of irregular visit intervals, while cross-mediator refinement provides additional gains in selected intervention-conditioned settings. Across real-world ADNI and simulator-generated ALPACA cohorts, CHDT shows improved long-horizon patient-state fidelity relative to competing baselines. Ablation results indicate that irregular-time conditioning provides the primary empirical gain, and cross-mediator refinement provides additional improvements.

title: Recycle only when you have to!
abstract: AlphaFold 3-like models (e.g., Boltz, Protenix, etc.) have pushed the frontier of protein binder design. This architecture is used both for the generation of binder candidates (e.g., by hallucination or converting these models into backbone or full atom generative models) as well as for the screening of these candidates for valid binders. In this paper, we start from the observation that AlphaFold 3's confidence metrics (ipSAE, ipTM) as well as structural consistency metrics can be predicted directly from the trunk even at early recycling. Because our proposed predictor is cheap, differentiable, and available at every cycle, it can be used in two distinct ways: as a decision signal to wisely spend the recycling budget for screening and as an objective for hallucination-based design. We show that both applications lead to increased performance at significantly reduced computational cost.

title: Physics-Grounded Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Molecular and Reaction Analysis in Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
abstract: Quantitative identification of molecular products and reaction pathways from scanning tunneling microscopy images is difficult when labeled images are unavailable for a new chemical system. We develop a simulation-assisted framework for zero-shot analysis that requires only precursor information for a new target system, with no experimental images or annotations from that system used during model training. The framework couples two functional components: NanoSim generates physics-grounded synthetic images from predicted reaction products and sampled surface scenes, while NanoAnalysis translates molecular detections into product populations, spatial arrangements, and mechanistic interpretations. Applied to a representative on-surface reaction, the detector achieves a micro-averaged F1 score of 0.92 on experimental images. Analysis of the detected molecules reveals annealing-dependent population changes and reaction-site preferences consistent with experimental observations. Beyond this capability, its modular organization allows heterogeneous data from other systems to be used to improve each component independently, providing a scalable route for continued generalization.

title: Tree-based Algorithms for Breakpoint Median and Near-Median Genomes
abstract: Median genomes serve as candidates for ancestral reconstruction and help study the diversity of parsimonious rearrangement solutions. However, the breakpoint median problem is NP-hard for unichromosomal genomes, and medians are non-unique, making their diversity important to study. In this paper, we develop tree-based algorithms for studying breakpoint medians of linear unichromosomal genomes represented as unsigned permutations. The algorithms construct rooted labeled trees whose leaves encode candidate median genomes satisfying local adjacency constraints derived from the inputs. We show that the resulting reduced search spaces contain all breakpoint medians while being much smaller than the full permutation space. We investigate these reduced spaces experimentally for three-genome instances. Our method finds exact medians and many near-optimal approximations, while early sampling of leaves often produces near-medians quickly. We also introduce constrained sampling procedures for targeting balanced near-medians, whose distances to the input genomes are more evenly distributed and hence are particularly relevant for ancestral reconstruction. The resulting framework provides a unified method for exact enumeration, efficient sampling, and targeted exploration of median and near-median genomes. In contrast to Traveling Salesman Problem-based approaches, which typically return a single solution and do not reveal the diversity or balance of the median set, our method can enumerate all medians, sample near-medians early, and target structurally distinct candidates under the breakpoint distance.

title: VitisGP: Multi-Task Benchmark for Genotype to Phenotype Grapevine Prediction
abstract: As climate change reshapes grape-growing conditions, predicting grapevine phenotypes from genomic variation is increasingly important for identifying and breeding cultivars suited to emerging environmental pressures. Existing research on the grapevine genotype-phenotype relationship using machine learning has often focused on individual traits, isolated regions, or a limited set of predictive models. We introduce VitisGP, a multi-phenotype curated dataset, integrating genome-wide SNP data with 26 heterogeneous phenotype prediction tasks spanning sommelier-curated aroma traits (N=11), botanical traits (N=14) and wine color---across 1,197 Vitis vinifera cultivars. We employ VitisGP to benchmark phenotype prediction, comparing machine-learning models with differing inductive biases---L2-regularized logistic regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, GBLUP and Transformer-based models, providing the first systematic comparison of this breadth on harmonized grapevine data. Across the benchmark, CatBoost achieves the strongest overall performance (macro-average AUROC=0.696 across 26 tasks), although model performance varies substantially across phenotype classes, with sensory and color traits showing stronger predictability than agronomic characteristics. VitisGP provides the community with a resource for investigating the genomic basis of phenotypic traits and screening grapevine diversity for climate-relevant characteristics.

title: Gravitational Lensing Signatures of a Black Hole in Mimetic Euler-Heisenberg theory
abstract: The present study delves into the gravitational lensing phenomena in the weak field limit of a charged black hole in the mimetic Euler-Heisenberg theory. The deflection angle of light is computed for the specified asymptotically flat spacetime assuming that the observer and the light source are both located at finite distances from the lens using the Gauss-Bonnet theorem. Additionally, the Einstein ring radius is analytically derived as a direct implementation of the deflection angle. The relevant influence of the Euler-Heisenberg parameter and the charge parameter on the Einstein ring radius is briefly discussed. We also investigate the observational implications of lensing in the weak gravitational limit of the black hole. The magnification and distortion parameter are also analyzed in this manuscript. Furthermore, the time delay of light due to gravitational lensing is also briefly discussed. Our study reveals the significant influence of the model parameters of the specified black hole on the gravitational lensing signatures.

title: The generalized core-EP inverse of operator matrices with generalized Schur complements
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the generalized core-EP inverse of block operator matrices over a Banach algebra. As a result, novel representations and explicit formulae for the core and core-EP inverses of the $2\times 2$ block operator matrices are established.

title: Which Adiabatic Cycles Alter an Action Variable?
abstract: Action variables are adiabatic invariants: their values are preserved during adiabatic time evolutions in completely integrable classical Hamiltonian systems. Nevertheless, an adiabatic cycle can alter how an action variable depends on phase-space variables that are independent of adiabatic parameters. Such a change, which we call action variable holonomy, induces adiabatic torus pumping in phase space. For a family of completely integrable kicked-top systems, a homotopy classification of adiabatic cycles identifies which adiabatic cycles induce action variable holonomy and adiabatic torus pumping. A physical example is also provided.

title: Moore-Postnikov supcation of simplicial sets and applications in simplicial algebras
abstract: We revisit a canonical filtration of simplicial algebras coming from the Moore-Postnikov system and provide several applications in studying the structure and classification of simplicial algebras and simplicial modules.

title: Descent and Decomposability of Algebras of Exponent 2 in characteristic 2
abstract: We define an invariant of central simple algebras of degree 8 and exponent 2 over fields of characteristic 2. It is built from the discriminant Pfister forms of symplectic involutions, takes values in a quotient of the third part of the graded group associated to the fundamental filtration of the Witt group of quadratic forms, and vanishes on tensor products of three quaternion algebras, thus giving a necessary condition for decomposability. Variants of the consctuction yield necessary and sufficient conditions for a biquaternion algebra to descend from a quadratic extension of the base field, and for a quaternion algebra to descent from a biquadratic extension that is not purely inseparable. Our results extend known results both in characteristic 2 and in characteristic different from 2, see the introduction. Using residue maps for quadratic forms, we show that these invariants do not vanish in general, and we give an explicit central simple algebra of degree 8 and exponent 2 with nonzero invariant, which is therefore indecomposable. As explained in the appendix, the purely inseparable case is quite different; in particular, a quaternion algebra descents if and only if its Brauer class also does.

title: DotSpace: A New Kind of Network for People and Their Agents
abstract: We introduce DotSpace, a network paradigm in which people and their agents participate as first-class members. Participants interact in persistent shared spaces, forming relationships, exchanging knowledge and taking action across ownership boundaries, while each owner retains authority over their own agents. In such a network, relationships can become channels for coordinated action: people and their agents share context, make decisions, create things and maintain ongoing commitments together, while their agents carry the work forward between people's visits. Our central proposition is that persistent networks of people and their agents can widen access to distributed capabilities and support increasingly complex collective activity. Over time, such networks may become environments in which knowledge, practices and capabilities develop, shaping both what participants can accomplish and how they organize their activity together.

title: Cutting out the middleman? Elon Musk and the rhetoric of citizen journalism in platform-mediated communication
abstract: This article examines how Elon Musk constructed discourse about journalism and the media on X between the 2024 United States presidential election and Donald Trump's presidential inauguration. It investigates how references to journalism, media organisations, and platform-based communication were articulated within Musk's posts, and how users responded to these narratives during a period of intense political polarisation. The study combines computational classification, qualitative thematic coding, and inferential statistical analysis. A corpus of 2,906 posts published by Musk between 5 November 2024 and 20 January 2025 was compiled. From this corpus, 500 posts referring to journalism, media organisations, platforms, or media-related discourse were identified through AI-assisted filtering and subsequent manual review. In addition, 42,066 user responses were analysed from a stratified sample drawn from 3,233,112 interactions. The analysis examined patterns of agreement and disagreement with Musk's stance and their relationship with thematic, gender, and professional variables inferred from publicly available profile information. The findings show that Musk's discourse is organised around three recurrent dynamics: criticism of institutional journalism, the association of media organisations with political and ideological agendas, and the presentation of X as an alternative communicative space. Journalism is predominantly framed through accusations of bias, disinformation, propaganda, and electoral manipulation, whereas X is more often linked to participation, innovation, and direct communication. User responses largely converged with Musk's position, although disagreement remained visible. While thematic orientation and professional background showed statistically significant associations with agreement patterns, effect sizes were limited.

title: Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model ($\text{DC}^2\text{SBM}$): A Generalized Structure Detection Method for Attributed Networks
abstract: Community detection in attributed networks is one of the core tasks of complex network analysis. The stochastic block model (SBM) and its variants are able to detect generalized network structures such as assortative, disassortative and mixed structures. However, existing generative methods either ignore node heterogeneity, or characterize node activity in the topological and attribute dimensions by one and the same factor, making it difficult to correctly model node activity when the two kinds of activity are decoupled. In this paper, we propose the Dual-Corrected Stochastic Block Model ($\text{DC}^2\text{SBM}$), which introduces independent correction factors---a topological degree factor and an attribute abundance factor---into the link-generation and attribute-generation channels, respectively, thereby effectively decoupling node activity from membership inference, and which further introduces a global scaling parameter to resolve the mismatch between the normalization constraints and the network scale. The model is inferred by the expectation--maximization (EM) algorithm, and the newly introduced factors cancel out completely in the posterior computation, so that no additional computational cost is incurred. Experiments on synthetic and real attributed networks show that DC^2SBM outperforms state-of-the-art methods in community detection accuracy, with an especially pronounced advantage when the topological signal is weak. The two correction factors can be recovered independently from their respective channels without cross-talk. Analytical as well as controlled experiments further demonstrate that modeling with a single shared factor fails when the two kinds of activity are decoupled---a regime that is prevalent in real networks---thereby validating the necessity of dual independent correction.

title: Asymmetric Decline Rather Than Backfire: A Repost-Network Analysis of Japanese Vaccine-Shedding Misinformation on X
abstract: This study investigates the diffusion of vaccine-shedding discourse on X in 2024, focusing on polarization in repost networks and reactions to corrective information. Here, "shedding" refers to the scientifically unsupported claim that harmful substances are released from individuals vaccinated against COVID-19 and cause adverse health effects in nearby unvaccinated people. Using 109,170 posts containing the Japanese term for "shedding" and 478,089 reposts collected from January 1 to December 31, 2024, we constructed a post-level repost network, identified discourse clusters, and examined changes in repost participation before and after major events. The results show that shedding discourse formed a two-pole structure consisting of pro-vaccine and anti-vaccine clusters. After news coverage denying shedding, we found no evidence of diffusion-level backfire in anti-vaccine repost activity. Instead, although the overall topic declined, repost participation in the anti-vaccine cluster decreased more sharply than that in the pro-vaccine cluster. User transition analysis further suggests that this change was not driven by the conversion of strongly anti-vaccine users, but by the entry of previously non-expressive users into pro-vaccine diffusion and the withdrawal of anti-vaccine supporters from repost activity. These findings suggest that corrective information may reshape the composition of misinformation diffusion participants without necessarily converting core opponents.

title: Beyond left-continuity: t-norms on the fuzzy unit interval induced by pairs of t-norms
abstract: We define a binary operation $T_1\star T_2$ on the fuzzy unit interval $\I$ by extending the natural action of $T_1$ and $T_2$ on step functions. When both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are left-continuous, this operation coincides with the tensor product of the corresponding quantales and therefore yields a t-norm on $\I$. Without left-continuity, the situation becomes more subtle. We prove that if at least one of the two t-norms is continuous, then $T_1\star T_2$ is still a t-norm on $\I$. We also show by counterexample that continuity cannot simply be dropped. The operation $\DN$ fails to be associative. On the other hand, $T_D\star T_D$ is a t-norm despite $T_D$ being neither continuous nor left-continuous, indicating that continuity is not a necessary condition.

title: The maximal determinant of order 15 over the third roots of unity
abstract: We prove that the largest absolute determinant of a $15\times15$ matrix with entries in $\{1,ω,ω^2\}$, where $ω^3=1$ and $ω\ne1$, is $120932352\sqrt{19}$. A matrix attaining this value was already known; the issue is maximality. The proof follows the Gram-matrix search method used in the real maximal-determinant problem. A sharp determinant bound in terms of the off-diagonal Gram energy, combined with Eisenstein congruences and a published classification of difference matrices, reduces a strict improvement to 23 possible energies. Componentwise Schur bounds and exact support catalogues then leave a small number of cases, excluded by orthogonality, rank, and spectral-intertwining conditions. We present the finite tests in a common framework and supply their replay programs. For the displayed extremizer we give a dephased representative, its Gram matrix and spectrum, and an exact computation of its monomial automorphism group, which has order 1008. The proof determines the value of the maximum, but does not classify all equality cases.

title: Centroids Of Partially Commutative Two-step Nilpotent Groups
abstract: In this paper, we describe the centroid (according to S. Lioutikov and A. Myasnikov) of an arbitrary finitely generated graph two-step nilpotent Hall exponential group over a binomial domain whose commutativity graph has no central vertices. Based on this description, we prove that if the non-commutativity graph of such a group has exactly one connected component and the group is non-Abelian, then the group is rigid.

title: Integration by differentiation
abstract: In this note, we address a traditional pedagogical asymmetry between algorithmic differentiation and heuristic integration by introducing an extra parametric-order differential framework. By treating the order of differentiation as a parametric axis (discrete or continuous), classical integration is reframed as a local differential evaluation at the non-positive boundary level. This analytical shift alleviates some traditional routines of integration by parts, by replacing the quadrature of a product of elementary functions with a direct differential series that either truncates into a finite algebraic sum or resolves through cyclic symmetries. This parametric-order approach also bridges the gap with fractional calculus, showing that non-integer derivatives emerge as a seamless extension of the same operational dimension. By reducing global quadrature to local differentiation, this note offers an efficient, conceptual tool for undergraduate analysis.

title: A Geometric View of Some Apportionment Paradoxes, Revisited
abstract: The Alabama paradox occurs when increasing the total number of seats in a legislature causes a state to lose a seat. We revisit a geometric analysis of this paradox published by Brent Bradberry in 1992, correct an erroneous probability formula, investigate the source of the error, and explore further consequences of the geometry.

title: A Winner Classification for Rooted Partizan Edge Geography on Heterogeneous Bouquets of Cycles
abstract: We consider an undirected edge-traversal game on a finite bouquet of simple cycles. Each of two players controls a token, both tokens begin at the common root, and the players alternate traversing edges that have not been used by either token. A player with no legal move loses. We prove that the first player wins precisely when the number of cycles of odd edge-length is odd, without assuming equal cycle lengths. The proof uses a simultaneous induction on root and defense configurations, with an exact analysis of the forced race between two opened cycles. We also explain how the classification corresponds to a completed Lean 4 formalization of the underlying game on finite edge sets.

title: Training for Alignment
abstract: We propose a simple model of training an agent with an endogenous bias. A principal chooses in which states to train the agent and what actions to prescribe in these states. In response, the agent updates their bias and then acts optimally given their new bias in untrained states, while following their training in trained states. The agent chooses their new bias to minimize a weighted average of their loss under their initial and final biases. Training can thus generalize to untrained states via the agent's bias updating. We characterize optimal training, which involves \emph{over-correction} in trained states and \emph{generalization-aware} (non-greedy) selection of training states. If only a small share of states can be trained, greedy state selection is approximately optimal, but over-correction remains essential. If any bias function is possible, or if the principal evaluates training robustly over bias functions that admit the possibility of full alignment, the value of training generalization vanishes, and greedy training becomes optimal. With a more pessimistic objective, \emph{under-correction}, or even no training at all, may be optimal. The principal benefits from the agent's preferences being more flexible (\emph{corrigibility}) when the set of possible biases is known and contains full alignment, but otherwise corrigibility can be harmful. Applications include socialization in organizations and families, and AI post-training and recursive self-improvement.

title: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations
abstract: Calibrating a cosmological simulation is an expensive, high-dimensional parameter optimization task. Previous works employ Bayesian optimization for automation, which treats the simulator as a black box and precludes the incorporation of human domain knowledge or workflow into the selection policy. We propose AgenticTuner, an agentic calibration pipeline with a present-day large language model serving as the optimizer who proposes the next parameter trial. We show that these agents can achieve competitive calibration performance at a fraction of the CPU cost when they are given informal, human-readable priors (such as codebase, documentation, and heuristic guides that seasoned scientists may possess). We hope this work serves as an early step toward AI scientists that can carry out complex, long-horizon scientific tasks.

title: Extended $\mathcal{O}$-operators on Lie-Yamaguti Algebras
abstract: We study balanced extended $\mathcal O$-operators on Lie--Yamaguti algebras. The construction links operator equations, algebra splittings and Yang--Baxter equations. We build a double from a representation and a balanced equivariant map. The graphs of extended $\mathcal O$-operators are exactly its subalgebras complementary to the first summand. We define extended post-Lie--Yamaguti algebras and prove their two-way relation with extended $\mathcal O$-operators. The tensor form gives a balanced extended Lie--Yamaguti Yang--Baxter equation. We construct a curved $L_\infty[1]$-algebra whose Maurer--Cartan elements are extended $\mathcal O$-operators. The normal representation of a graph gives a cohomology theory for infinitesimal deformations, rigidity and obstructions. We include both cyclic conditions in the lowest paired degree. We also map operator infinitesimals to the deformation cohomology of the induced algebra. Examples give obstructed infinitesimals, rigid scalar operators and nontrivial formal deformations.

title: Urban Mobility and Demand Dynamics: A Telemetry and Ticketing Baseline for Niteroi's Bus Network
abstract: The public transportation networks of rapidly expanding urban centers confront a complex task in balancing operational efficiency with dynamic commuter needs. In response, data-driven approaches leveraging multi-perspective datasets offer critical insights into a city's systemic demand. In this work, we utilize the NetMob 2026 Data Challenge dataset for the city of Niteroi, Brazil, to investigate the structural dynamics of the municipal bus network. Specifically, our research framework is driven by three interconnected urban mobility objectives: first, analyzing urban movement patterns to determine whether passenger boarding logs trace periodic, routine, and predictable movement patterns across distinct urban zones; second, detecting operational anomalies and potential bottlenecks by analyzing vehicle trajectory profiles via GPS telemetry to identify both scheduled and unscheduled stops; and third, developing and evaluating a supervised learning framework capable of predicting continuous bus trip durations.

title: The Bi-LF Positive Conjecture Holds
abstract: We prove that a semidomain has length-factorial additive and multiplicative monoids if and only if it is isomorphic to the semiring of nonnegative integers or is a unique factorization domain. Consequently, bi-length-factoriality and bi-factoriality coincide for all semidomains, settling the Bi-LF Positive Conjecture. The main step shows that additive length-factoriality and multiplicative factoriality force additive factoriality, without an additive reducedness assumption. Multiplicative factoriality forces every semidomain with a nonzero additive unit to be a unique factorization domain. In the additively reduced case, a uniform multiplier for lattice points in a finitely generated cone yields cancellation of divisibility across sums, which leads to an obstruction to additive atoms dividing positive integers and completes the structural argument. We also consider related questions on quasi-factoriality and classify the rational and transcendental monogenic positive semirings whose multiplicative monoids are quasi-$n$-factorial for a prescribed integer $n \ge 2$.

title: Accurate structural identification for layered composite structures, through a wave and finite element scheme
abstract: We present for the first time an approach for identifying the geometric and material characteristics of layered composite structures through an inverse wave and finite element approach. More specifically, this Non-Destructive Evaluation (NDE) approach is able to recover the thickness, density, as well as all independent mechanical characteristics such as the tensile and shear moduli for each layer of the composite structure under investigation. This is achieved through multi-frequency single shot measurements. It is emphasized that the success of the approach is independent of the employed excitation frequency regime, meaning that both structural dynamics and ultrasound frequency spectra can be employed. It is demonstrated that more efficient convergence of the identification process is attained closer to the bending-to-shear transition range of the layered structure. Since a full FE description is employed for the periodic composite, the presented approach is able to account for structures of arbitrary complexity. The procedure is applied to a sandwich panel with composite facesheets and results are compared with two wave-based characterization techniques: the Inhomogeneous Wave Correlation method and the Transition Frequency Characterization method. Numerical simulations and experimental results are presented to verify the robustness of the proposed method.

title: Point-to-ellipse series -- Part II Expansion about the center
abstract: Power series expansions in the polar distance about the center are derived for the normal direction and signed distance from an ellipse to points near its center. After extracting constant terms and common factors, the series coefficients are polynomials in the axis ratio and the absolute value of the sine of the polar angle, with rational coefficients. The region of convergence is shown to be the region bounded by the ellipse evolute. The expansions complement previously derived expansions valid for points far from the center.

title: Sharp bounds, stability, and arithmetic fluctuations for induced pentagons
abstract: We prove that every graph with $m>0$ edges contains at most $\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}(\frac{m}{5})^{5/2}$ induced pentagons. Equality holds precisely for balanced blow-ups of the Clebsch graph, together with isolated vertices. The bound and equality classification extend to arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights and to all graphons, including fractional graphons. Moreover, a deficit of $\varepsilon$ in the normalized ratio can be repaired by $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon}m)$ edge edits on the original vertex set, producing an exactly balanced Clebsch blow-up and isolates. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal. We further separate the linear cost of adjacency errors from the quadratic cost of class imbalance. This yields an arithmetic description of the finite-edge deficit and its explicit second-order term, with a uniform power-saving remainder. For each fixed integer $j$, the exact extremal count at $m=40k^2+j$ is eventually an integer coefficient polynomial in $k$, computable by a finite enumeration; we do not quantify its threshold of validity. The proof combines global variational conditions, an active-density bound, and an exact rational certificate on the $1,044$ graphs of order seven. A positive-slope identity permits a single rational reference density. An exact conditional span excludes triangles at equality, after which degree and codegree identities determine the Clebsch structure. All finite certificates admit independent verification using integer arithmetic.

title: CausalGrade: Evidence-Guided Causal Graph Scoring with Jev
abstract: Evaluating the structural quality of candidate causal graphs when the true causal structure is unknown is an important problem in applying causal discovery results. This paper proposes CausalGrade, a causal graph scoring method based on the probabilistic judgment model Jev. The method jointly provides Jev with evidence of association, conditional dependence, and directionality from observational data and edge probabilities produced by the causal discovery foundation model CDFM. Jev produces probabilistic judgments about direct causal edges, and a graph-level score is obtained by measuring the agreement between the adjacency structure of the graph under evaluation and these edge-level judgments. Across 300 synthetic datasets, the score exhibits a relatively strong negative correlation with structural error in all 20 combinations of four causal discovery algorithms and five variable counts, indicating that higher scores generally correspond to smaller structural errors. In 500 synthetic graph selection tasks, CausalGrade achieves a best-candidate hit rate of 54.4\%, exceeding the 48.4\% achieved by the Self-Compatibility metric \(κ_G\), further supporting its ability to discriminate the structural quality of graphs under evaluation.

title: Finite-Element Electromagnetic Analysis and Evaluation of Antenna Performance Metrics Using a Quantum Linear System Solver
abstract: Electromagnetic analysis based on the finite element method is widely used in antenna design. At higher frequencies, however, the required mesh refinement makes solving large sparse linear systems the main contributor to computational cost. Quantum linear system solvers offer a potential means of accelerating this step, but their output is a superposition state: reconstructing all components of the classical solution vector would forfeit the quantum speedup. Prior studies have proposed methods for obtaining physical quantities such as scattering cross sections and scattering parameters from the solution state. To support antenna design using fault-tolerant quantum computers, we formulate the total radiated power, the radiated power within a prescribed solid angle, and the dielectric and conductive losses as observables for efficient evaluation from a quantum solution state. These observables avoid the measurement cost of reconstructing all components of the output quantum state. We develop an end-to-end hybrid quantum--classical workflow that combines finite-element electromagnetic analysis, matrix preconditioning, a quantum linear system solver, and the evaluation of antenna design metrics. To validate the workflow, we performed numerical experiments evaluating these observables for an axisymmetric coaxially fed monopole antenna. Under idealized conditions, the relative errors in the total radiated power and the dissipated power with respect to the classical finite-element solution were on the order of $10^{-3}$, confirming the consistency of the workflow. The proposed method is expected to provide a basis for using quantum linear system solvers to evaluate antenna performance and, in the future, to design high-frequency wireless devices.

title: Four runners that are barely lonely
abstract: For positive integers $v_1,\dots,v_n$ let $\mathrm{ML}(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\max_t\min_i\|v_it\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer. Kravitz asked which values below $1/n$ occur. For $n=4$, Jain and Kravitz showed that the values below $1/4$ are $m/(4m+2)$, $m\ge2$, up to finitely many undetermined exceptions. We settle the four-runner case completely. A primitive quadruple has $\mathrm{ML}<1/4$ if and only if it is, up to order, $\{1,2,3,4k\}$, or $\{x,y,x+y,x+2y\}$ with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y\not\equiv x,2x\pmod 4$, or $\{1,3,4,14\}$. The values below $1/4$ are exactly $m/(4m+2)$ with $m\ge2$, $m\ne3$, so $3/14$ is the only exception, and Conjecture 4.1 of Fan and Sun holds. A density lemma bounds the length of a quadruple on neither critical subtorus by $512$, and an exact search over 800,816,099 quadruples completes the proof. The same method shows that the two-dimensional subtori of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^4$ with loneliness below $2/5$ take exactly the three-runner values in that range, which between $1/3$ and $2/5$ are the fractions $p/q$ with $1\le 2q-5p\le 4$. Hence the accumulation points of the four-runner spectrum in $(0,2/5]$ are the three-runner values there, as Giri and Kravitz conjectured, and $9/25$ is not the loneliness of a two-dimensional subtorus. For every $n$, assuming the conjecture for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, we prove $\mathrm{ML}(v)>1/n-(n(n-1))^{n-2}/(2|v|)$, which is sharp in $|v|$, and that every $n$-tuple with $\mathrm{ML}<1/n$ and $|v|\ge n(n(n-1))^{2n-4}$ lies on a two-dimensional subtorus of loneliness $1/n$. This answers a question of Cordella. For five speeds, a two-dimensional subtorus of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^5$ with loneliness below $2/9$ is the product of a coordinate circle with the circle of $\{1,2,3,4\}$ or $\{1,3,4,7\}$. We also give infinitely many subtori whose maximizers lie off every circle with a repeated speed.

title: JYVA at BeTraC: Audio-Based Medical Note Generation with SOAP Section-Specific Queries
abstract: We present our submission to the Beyond Transcription Challenge (BeTraC) on medical note generation from doctor-patient audio conversations. We propose a section-aware approach based on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, in which a lightweight Q-Former learns SOAP section-specific queries to extract compact clinical representations from speech. In the lightweight track, our system ranks fourth and substantially outperforms the challenge baseline, achieving a Concept F1 of 0.5005 on the official test set. The organizers' analysis and our heuristic evaluation suggest improved robustness to hallucinations, and better stability under difficult audio conditions. These results show that explicitly modeling SOAP structure through section-specific queries is an effective way to improve the faithfulness and reliability of audio-based medical note generation.

title: Asymptotic stability of clique-saturating edges near Turán thresholds
abstract: Let $f_{p+1}(n,m)$ denote the minimum number of $K_{p+1}$-saturating edges in an $n$-vertex $K_{p+1}$-free graph with $m$ edges. In this paper, we investigate the stability of this parameter near the Turán thresholds, with particular emphasis on the role of the minimum degree. We introduce the refined parameter $f_{p+1,p}(n,m,δ)$. It is defined for $K_{p+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, minimum degree $δ$, and containing at least a copy of $K_p$. For every fixed integer $p\ge3$, we establish a stability result when the number of edges is $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2)$, showing that \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,δ)=\left(\frac{(p-2)^2}{2(p-1)^3}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2), \ δ\geq \left(\frac{p-2}{p-1}+o(1)\right)n. \] We further obtain a stability theorem in the regime where the number of edges is quadratically smaller than $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})$. More precisely, for $0 \leq c< \frac{1}{2p(3p-1)}$, \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,δ)=\left(\frac{1}{2p}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})-(c+o(1))n^2, \ δ\geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}-2c+o(1)\right)n. \]

title: Optimal Sampling and Noise Mitigation for Vocal Fold Kinematics in High-Speed Videoendoscopy
abstract: Objectives: High-Speed Videoendoscopy glottal area waveforms conflate lateral fold excursion with longitudinal opening, precluding direct estimation of velocity, acceleration, and left-right asymmetry. Displacement waveforms preserve these quantities but are susceptible to spatial quantization and temporal sampling errors. We characterize these errors, evaluate reduction via Kalman smoothing and temporal interpolation, and determine optimal frame rate bounds relative to pixel excursion, speed quotient (SQ), and open quotient (OQ). Methods: Sampling theory was used to derive analytical frame-rate bounds required for kinematic feature fidelity. Kalman smoothing was compared with FFT-based denoising, paired with sinc or spline interpolation. Interpolation was evaluated on 4000 fps recordings (N=55) downsampled and reconstructed. A 16000 fps dataset (N=12) served as reference for noise reduction across 2000-8000 fps downsampled waveforms evaluated on peak displacement, velocity, OQ, and SQ. Results: Sinc interpolation yielded lower median mean absolute error than spline (0.29 vs 0.52 pixels), with 85% of recordings (47/55) versus 45% (25/55) below 0.5 pixels. For kinematic feature estimation (N=12), Kalman-sinc outperformed FFT-sinc in 75% of feature-by-frame-rate pairings. Conclusion: Computing kinematic features without artifacts requires joint consideration of temporal and spatial resolution. Kalman-sinc preprocessing at 8000 fps is recommended for velocity and SQ measures. Peak lateral displacement can be measured at 2000 fps, while OQ requires 4000 fps for typical spatial resolutions (9-14 pixels maximum excursion). Pixel excursion should be reported alongside kinematic measures to contextualize data reliability.

title: A Diophantine generalization of Fourier's irrationality trick
abstract: We revisit Fourier's method for proving the irrationality of $e$ and generalize it into a unified Diophantine framework, which applies to a broad class of series with bounded or mildly growing integer numerators, and suitably growing, divisible denominators. Using integer linear forms, we establish a general criterion that recovers classical irrationality results while also generating new ones within a single structural approach.

title: CalibCause: A Quality-Gated, Interpretable and Calibrated Deep Learning Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
abstract: Most deep learning systems for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading are evaluated on a single data source, with limited evidence of cross-site generalisation, uncertainty calibration, and interpretability. We propose CalibCause, a quality-gated mixture-of-experts framework that combines per-expert visual explanations, label-free image-quality conditioning, knowledge distillation, and calibrated confidence with deferral. We evaluated the framework using 51,310 fundus images from EyePACS, DDR, and APTOS 2019, with IDRiD and DeepDRiD for external testing. Evaluation included pooled testing, leave-one-environment-out experiments, paired bootstrap confidence intervals, and local grade-threshold adaptation. On the pooled test split, the label-free distilled student achieved quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.863 and accuracy of 0.865 with 27.8 million parameters, 52% fewer than its teacher. Across held-out environments, the label-free model achieved mean QWK of 0.741 compared with 0.743 for a plain ConvNeXt-Tiny baseline, while adversarial invariance did not improve cross-site grading accuracy. Refitting grade thresholds using 200 labelled images increased held-out EyePACS QWK from 0.533 to 0.621 for the label-free model. After vector scaling, expected calibration error ranged from 0.025 to 0.036 across CalibCause variants, and deferring the least confident 20% of images increased student accuracy from 0.865 to 0.923 on the remaining images. These findings demonstrate that quality-aware grading, interpretable expert routing, model compression, and calibrated deferral can be integrated without sacrificing cross-site performance relative to a plain baseline, although reliable deployment still requires local validation and adaptation.

title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
abstract: To rigorously establish the value of a novel deep learning method, it must be compared against appropriate baselines. As deep learning has become increasingly common in the physical and life sciences, there have been numerous cases in which apparent progress has turned out to be an artifact of omitted or missing baselines. In this work, we investigate whether this problem can be mitigated by using large language models to automate the construction of baselines. We assemble 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals that investigate novel deep learning methods for scientific applications. We then use a language model to construct simple baselines for each task. These automatically constructed baselines are strong, recovering a median of 95.5% (mean 85.7%) of the gap between a trivial predictor and the score of the deep learning model. The median simple baseline matches or exceeds the performance of the deep learning model in 12 studies. We further examine the variation across scientific domains and publication venues and we characterize the effects of test-time compute and access to different levels of study context. As human peer review has struggled to keep up with the rapidly increasing volume of research articles in recent years, our results suggest that automated baseline construction is a practical and scalable check on deep learning contributions in the physical and life sciences.

title: FGSM Attack Transferability from Simulation to Quantum Hardware in Network Intrusion Detection
abstract: Quantum computers are now available through cloud platforms, and recent work has proposed using them to detect network intrusions. It is not yet clear how easily such systems can be attacked. We train a hybrid variational quantum classifier (VQC) on the Friday DDoS subset of CICIDS2017 and test it against two attacks: label flipping during training and FGSM evasion at prediction time. We run the tests in simulation and on IBM hardware, the Fez superconducting processor (Heron r2). We find that two models with similar accuracy can differ greatly in how easily they are attacked. A model that decides with little confidence loses half its detections to a very small change in the input, while a model trained to decide with more confidence needs a much larger change before it fails. Attacks built in simulation against the more confident model also work on real hardware, and the device classifies every unaltered attack sample correctly. Simulated device noise does not reduce accuracy, but it does reduce the model's confidence and makes attacks easier, so accuracy alone does not show how exposed a model is. Label flipping has no measurable effect until 15% of attack labels are changed. These results show that device noise should not be treated as a defense and that reported weaknesses in these classifiers depend partly on how they were trained.

title: Anchored Fusion for Automated Airway Segmentation in Pediatric and Adult CT
abstract: Airway segmentation from chest CT enables branch-level measurement of airway size and growth, but peripheral bronchi remain hard to segment, particularly in children, whose airways are smaller and for whom few annotated scans exist. Different models recover complementary branches of the airway tree. Their union improves overall tree coverage but also introduces disconnected non-airway objects. We propose anchored fusion (A-Fuse), which takes the voxel-wise union of TfeNet, a retrained MEDPSeg and a reimplemented AirMorph and retains the connected component with greatest overlap with the AirMorph mask. On 30 held-out adult CTs from the ATM'26 training set, A-Fuse reaches a Dice score of 93.24% and the highest branch detection rate among compared methods (92.05%). On nine pediatric scans, it reaches 94.15% Dice and 68.79% branch detection. A-Fuse retains the airway tree in all 39 test scans, whereas keeping the largest component selects a non-airway object in four. A-Fuse is deployed as an automated web application and we release all code, trained weights and an open-source ITK-SNAP extension for 3D tubular segmentation editing.

title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Using two results from Fourier's preprint, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these values of $k$. The second version of Fourier's preprint gives an independent proof of this statement. For $k=1$, the equality statement is false: the polytopes $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have the same number of edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. Together with Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. The proofs given in this paper are formally verified in Lean 4.

title: Mpemba effect as an entropy-production race:Finite-amplitude bounds on crossing times in Markovian relaxation
abstract: Two canonical preparations evolving under a common final Markov generator can exhibit the Mpemba effect because they excite different relaxation modes. We bound the first crossing of their relative entropies by treating relaxation as an entropy-production race. The exact balance $-\dot D=\dot e_p$ implies that a meeting occurs when the accumulated \emph{difference} of normalized entropy-production rates, $\int_0^t(r_H-r_C)\,\mathrm ds$ with $r_α=\dot e_p^α/D_α$, equals the initial logarithmic deficit $\ln[D_H(0)/D_C(0)]$. Global entropy-decay inequalities yield a lower crossing-time bound when the entropy-decay constant is bounded from below and the hot rate from above; we supply both certificates. A nonzero cubic moment of a slowest eigenfunction is sufficient for the modified logarithmic Sobolev constant to lie strictly below the spectral gap. Combining established relative-entropy comparison inequalities with Markov contraction and the actual mode amplitudes gives finite-amplitude crossing bounds without a small-deviation expansion. For an exactly strong, reversible three-state preparation these give $0.1659\le t_M\le0.1674$ in model time units, independently certified by outward-rounded interval arithmetic. This interval is narrower than $1\%$ and contains $t_M=0.1662209$. The conservative global-rate comparison used here gives only $t_M\ge0.042$. The hotter preparation starts $6.12$ times farther from equilibrium, yet it reaches $D=10^{-5}$ at $t=0.233$, compared with $t=0.844$ for the colder one. Mean energy crosses later than relative entropy. For a fixed driven generator, nonadiabatic entropy production governs the same balance. These results concern finite-state relaxation in a specified distance and do not predict water-freezing times.

title: DiffUltra: Task-Guided Pathology Synthesis for Large-Scale Real-World Lung Ultrasound Data
abstract: Despite their scale, large medical imaging datasets may underrepresent clinically relevant pathological presentations. Synthetic data can expand coverage, but findings must remain compatible with surrounding anatomy. This is challenging in ultrasound, where findings resemble surrounding tissue and must be positioned relative to anatomical landmarks. We propose DiffUltra, a task-guided latent diffusion pipeline that models pathological structure and spatial context, and screens synthetic images for downstream utility. DiffUltra conditions generation on structural masks decomposing findings into anechoic, hypoechoic, and hyperechoic subregions. Two placement strategies insert findings into pathology-absent backgrounds or replace existing findings with structurally matched pathology from other patients. A filter trained exclusively on real data retains images whose predictions agree spatially with target boxes. We evaluate DiffUltra for lung ultrasound detection of pleural effusion and consolidation, using over 700,000 expert-annotated frames from 598 patients at 12 sites. Averaged across three real-data scales, synthetic insertion significantly improved video-level AUROC for both pleural effusion (p = 0.017) and consolidation (p < 0.01). For pleural effusion, frame-level average precision improved by 4.5 percentage points on average and by 6.1 points using only 10% of real data (p < 0.01 for both). Synthetic insertion also yielded larger average precision gains than an existing diffusion-based lesion-insertion method at every scale. At full scale, targeted synthesis improved AUROC for both pathologies by 1.1-3.9 points in an underrepresented anatomical zone and on a held-out acquisition system. These results suggest that anatomically constrained, task-guided synthesis can help address coverage gaps in ultrasound training data.

title: TheseusSyn: Unified Medical Image Synthesis via Context-Conditioned Masked Autoregression
abstract: High-fidelity medical image synthesis is promising for data-efficient learning and privacy-preserving model development. However, most existing approaches rely on symbolic or label-based conditioning, which constrains generative diversity and limits case-specific contextual fidelity. Inspired by the Ship of Theseus paradox, we propose TheseusSyn, a novel context-conditioned synthesis paradigm that generates images through iterative content replacement. Our framework employs a multi-codebook discrete tokenizer to convert medical images into sequences of token indices, extracted with a global representation token that serves as a contextual constraint. A masked autoregressive generative model then iteratively masks and predicts tokens conditioned on both local neighborhoods and the global context. By progressively replacing image content until the entire token sequence is renewed, TheseusSyn produces synthetic samples that preserve anatomical coherence and semantic consistency while introducing controlled diversity. We evaluate the proposed framework on multiple datasets from MedMNIST by constructing synthetic datasets with varying masking strategies and training ResNet-18 classifiers exclusively on either real or synthetic data. Experimental results demonstrate that classifiers trained on TheseusSyn-generated images achieve competitive performance on official test sets, indicating that the synthesized data preserve diagnostically relevant features and semantic consistency. Systematic analysis of masking strategies reveals their impact on structural fidelity and downstream classification accuracy. These results suggest that context-conditioned masked autoregression provides an effective and generalizable solution for label-free medical image synthesis, offering a scalable alternative to conventional data augmentation and class-conditioned generative models in medical imaging applications.

title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.

title: Report-Derived Labels, an Image Teacher and the Gap to Expert Labels in Knee MRI: An Analysis of One Entry to the RSNA 2026 Knee Abnormality Detection Challenge
abstract: In the RSNA 2026 Knee Abnormality Detection challenge, 58 of 4,407 training studies have expert labels for 12 findings, and the rest have only a radiology report. We compare training targets built from a language-model reading of the reports and from a public image model against two references: the expert labels and the 39,248 study-finding cells that the reports state as present or absent. The report labels and the out-of-fold predictions of the image model reach similar agreement with the expert labels (macro AUC 0.892 and 0.896) but fail on different findings. The report is better for ligament tears and patellofemoral osteoarthritis, which it never calls present when the experts do not; the image model is better for effusion, Baker's cyst, contusion, and synovitis, where the reports call the finding absent, leave it out, or call it present more often than the experts. Their equal mixture reaches 0.927 (gain over the report labels 0.035, 95% interval 0.019 to 0.052), also after removing the studies whose knee side was handled inconsistently. We did not observe a model-level gain from this better target: a 2.5D ResNet50 trained on the report labels alone scored 0.877 on the private leaderboard, after the deadline, against 0.872 for the same model trained on the mixture, and the out-of-fold advantage of the mixture is confounded by a change of code and by possible leakage through the image model's folds. A scanner prevalence prior raised agreement with the reports but not with the experts, so a report-derived reference can reward reporting habits. A rank correction for co-occurring findings gave small out-of-fold gains and no visible leaderboard effect. Our entry, a forked public ensemble with that correction, was displayed at rank 582 of 6,299 on the private leaderboard (0.943, a score shared by 287 teams). All results are exploratory; none of the models is meant for clinical use.

title: Finite-resource cooling of qudits beyond thermodynamic length
abstract: Cooling a quantum system with $N$ thermal machines costs more than Landauer's bound.
