For swap-based collision models the excess is set by thermodynamic length, which is optimal for qubits and was suggested by numerics to be optimal in general. We show that for qudits, permutations of energy eigenstates that use several resonant transitions at once do better for every spectrum, reducing the excess by up to 83% near the ground state. To second order, coherent collisions do no better, and at infinite temperature $d_M$-level machines reduce the excess by at most a factor $d_M-1$.

title: Cross-Device Transfer of a Hospital-Trained Fetal Head Circumference Model to a Low-Cost Handheld Ultrasound Probe
abstract: Automated fetal head circumference (HC) measurement reaches near-expert accuracy on the HC18 benchmark, but published models are trained and evaluated on hospital-grade equipment. We quantify what happens when such a model is carried to a low-cost handheld probe. A lightweight segmentation network (CSM, 0.13M parameters) was trained on HC18 across five independent runs and applied without modification to images from a $1,350 handheld probe (SonoQue C3), acquired at the same visit as the reference hospital scan in 18 patients. In-domain accuracy was 2.34 +/- 0.43 mm; on handheld images the same model gave 16.12 mm against the hospital record, a 6.9-fold degradation. Input preprocessing, a choice rarely reported, accounted for about a third of that gap: direct resizing gave 49.45 mm against 16.12 mm for an aspect-preserving pipeline. A leave-one-out data-efficiency curve showed that fine-tuning on two images significantly worsened accuracy, and that from four images upward error fell by 0.75 mm per doubling of the local dataset (p = 0.0045), although no training-set size up to 27 images significantly improved on the unmodified model. Much of the residual gap belongs to the reference rather than the model: scored against a manual tracing of the same image the model was already within 10.48 mm, and its disagreement with sonographer calipers on the same frame was a near-constant offset, negative in 10 of 10 cases. A single calibration constant estimated leave-one-out reduced that disagreement from 8.12 mm to 3.49 mm, reaching the intraobserver reproducibility reported for experienced sonographers, but did not improve agreement with the hospital record. Cross-device evaluations should therefore report the input preprocessing used and characterise the precision of their reference standard.

title: Thin-shell wormholes from magnetic black holes in exponential electrodynamics
abstract: Transparent magnetic wormholes can share a black hole exterior while their supporting matter controls the response of the throat. We construct symmetric thin shells from the magnetic black hole of exponential nonlinear electrodynamics and derive their equilibrium stresses and linear radial stability criterion. Restricting the seed to its zero-bare-mass magnetic branch ties the charge and coupling along the fixed-mass family. In sampled cases, calibrated linear barotropic shells are unstable, whereas variable phantom and variable Chaplygin laws admit locally stable radial sectors. Explicit radius dependence strengthens the phantom restoring term; the Chaplygin response cancels the divergent inverse lapse contribution and permits stable sectors close to a non-extremal seed horizon. The surface density remains negative, although an inner interval satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. At the seed photon sphere, the two variable laws share an exact stabilization threshold. The complete radial averaged null energy remains negative even when the proper shell energy tends to zero. Numerical null geodesic imaging uses independent, minimally coupled light and transparent junctions, with celestial sources and rotating thin disks truncated at the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO). For observer-side disk emission with the prescribed ISCO truncation and a throat below the seed photon sphere, inclined images coincide with the seed black hole image. A throat above that sphere removes selected returning contributions while preserving much of the bright primary structure. Illuminating the opposite exterior adds inner disk arcs, but a central dark region can survive because the disk does not illuminate every transmitted direction. Image degeneracy depends jointly on the retained null trajectories and the emitting support, rather than on the presence of a horizon alone.

title: Anti-concentration and Graham's rearrangement problem in finite abelian groups
abstract: Let $S$ be a subset of $n$ elements of a group $G$. An ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of its elements is valid if the partial sums $x_1,x_1+x_2,\ldots,x_1+\cdots+x_n$ are pairwise distinct. This notion has a long history in combinatorial group theory, dated back to Gordon's works in early 1960. Alspach-Liversidge conjecture asserts that any subset of the nonzero elements of a finite abelian group $G$ has a valid ordering. This generalizes Graham's conjecture, which considers the case when the group $G$ is $\mathbb{F}_p$, the cyclic group of prime order. Graham's conjecture has been solved recently, as a combination of results by Kravitz, Bedert and Kravitz, Müyesser and Pokrovskiy, Bedert, Bucić, Kravitz, Montgomery, and Müyesser, and Pham and Sauermann. Beside this, the only other case where Alspach-Liversidge conjecture has been confirmed is $G=\mathbb{F}_2^k$, thanks to a recent result by Bedert, Bucić, Kravitz, Montgomery, and Müyesser. We prove the Alspach-Liversidge conjecture in its full generality. Our proof combines ideas from many previous papers. In particular, we will use the probabilistic approach and the absorption method. Our new main technical ingredient is a Fourier-moment estimate, which is of independent interest. In particular, we can use it to show that the distribution of certain kinds of random sums in an abelian group has an almost uniform distribution.

title: The Geometry of Multitask Learning: Sharp Rates for Shared Subspace Estimation
abstract: Learning a shared subspace in multitask learning is an important statistical problem, yet exact rates remain poorly understood in many of the formal settings considered in the literature. To address this gap, which arises from limitations of existing upper-bound techniques, we propose a general multitask lemma. The lemma provides sufficient conditions for fast subspace estimation in generic multitask settings, in the form of geometric conditions on the task regression functions and their estimators. We subsequently show that the multitask lemma yields sharp minimax rates---previously unknown---for linear regression and classification in the regimes considered, and rates matching up to logarithmic factors for additive-noise regression.

title: PrivacyFlow: Privacy in AI Agents through Information Flow Analysis and Consequence-Aware Risk Management
abstract: Autonomous LLM agents executing multi-step workflows over personal data often misalign with user privacy expectations and leak sensitive, out-of-context information. Although Contextual Integrity (CI) formalizes this problem, existing benchmarks and defenses rarely operationalize CI for realistic multi-step task sequences in evolving environments. In this work, we first introduce agentic PrivacyBench, a benchmark of 5873 tasks in 986 task sequences with dynamic environment updates and CI-grounded allow-sets for sensitive information. We also introduce PrivacyFlow, a defense that separates deliberative privacy planning (System 2) from task execution (System 1), treating each sharing decision as a structured risk-management problem. Before execution, PrivacyFlow traces the provenance and purpose of each planned data flow, models recipient background knowledge, and simulates what external actors could infer. This allows us to model the downstream consequences of disclosure, including inference attacks and context-dependent harms. It then weighs the remaining disclosure risk against task utility and executes a minimized plan, blocks it, or consults the user. Across six models, PrivacyFlow significantly reduces step-level privacy failures and raises the share of completed task sequences without a detected privacy violation by 22--55 percentage points. We further highlight a new privacy--utility--autonomy tradeoff: allowing PrivacyFlow to proactively prompt the user in case of uncertainty can increase authorized task completion at the cost of shifting decision effort back to the user. Our results suggest that proactive CI reasoning can substantially improve agentic privacy and motivate further study of this tradeoff.

title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
abstract: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.

title: Characterizing LLM Agent Behaviors in Module Shadowing Environments
abstract: LLM agents operating in untrusted workspaces face the risk of untrusted code execution during routine tasks, yet final reports and workspace states alone cannot reliably establish whether execution occurred. We introduce an evaluation framework that codes observation, reasoning, execution, and response behaviors from agent trajectories and aligns them with independent environmental records to reconstruct execution histories and verify final reports. We apply this framework to module shadowing, in which a local file is loaded in place of a trusted module during import, enabling untrusted code execution without adversarial prompts. Across 90 trials with 15 models, the payload executed in 51% of direct shadowing trials and 87% of indirect shadowing trials. Even explicit recognition of the shadowing mechanism did not ensure prevention, as the payload ran in 10 of the 29 trials with recorded recognition. These failures were often omitted from final reports, as 49 of the 62 triggered trials ended without mention of the security issue. Three reports even denied execution, including one from a trial in which independent logs recorded 19 payload executions. Final workspace states also obscured prior execution when agents deleted or overwrote the payload marker in 10 triggered trials. These findings demonstrate that combining behavioral coding with independent environmental auditing enables rigorous and transparent evaluation of agent safety.

title: CS-LDM: Clinically Guided Structure-Aware Latent Diffusion for Knee Radiographic Forecasting
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a leading cause of physical disability and currently has no curative clinical treatment. Early diagnosis and accurate prognosis are therefore vital for managing its progression. Existing methods mainly predict future severity grades and provide limited visual explanation of structural change. Recent generation-guided approaches synthesize follow-up radiographs for progression assessment, but generated images are often judged by predictive accuracy or image realism, so they may satisfy a grading model while remaining morphologically unreliable. We therefore propose CS-LDM, a clinically guided, structure-aware latent diffusion framework that forecasts patient-specific future knee radiographs from the current X-ray and clinically available current KL grade, using LoRA adaptation, current-grade conditioning, and frozen-teacher diagnostic distillation. Experiments on the public Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) dataset show that CS-LDM improves future severity-grade consistency while maintaining competitive image fidelity. Further ordinal, OARSI, ROI-level, and stable/progressed analyses show that radiographic forecasting should be evaluated by balancing diagnostic consistency, anatomical plausibility, and structural preservation.

title: Bernstein and Stieltjes properties of some functions involving logarithmic functions
abstract: We show that $\frac1{g(x)}$, with $g(x)=\frac{x-1}{x\ln x}$, is a complete Bernstein function and give its Lévy measure explicitly. For $h(x)=\frac{(x^2-1)\ln(x+1)}{x^2\ln x}$, we prove that $h$ is not a Stieltjes function, so $\frac1h$ is not a complete Bernstein function, but $\frac1h$ is a Bernstein function. The latter rests on the positivity of a function built from the convolution of the exponential integrals $E_1$ and $E_2$. We also give a related completely monotonic function that is not a Stieltjes function.

title: Weak Identification in Bunching Designs: Rare Events and Counterfactual Uncertainty
abstract: We study shrinking tax kinks when the counterfactual density is locally Hölder continuous and may be accompanied by a known background atom at the threshold. Small policy incentives create two distinct obstacles: few behavioral bunchers and an unobserved relocation interval. For the complete observed distribution, we establish matching minimax bounds for elasticity estimation and honest confidence-set diameter. With kink size $d$, background mass $γ$, and smoothness $0<s\leq1$, the rate is $\min\{1,\sqrt{(γ+d)/(nd^2)}+d^s\}$. The stochastic component has a rare-event scale when the background mass is of the kink order or smaller and a conventional weak-signal scale when it remains positive. The extrapolation component follows from observationally equivalent counterfactual densities, rather than sampling error. We derive normal and Poisson limits for a conventional bunching ratio, show a coverage failure of its Wald interval, and give finite-sample confidence sets by exact binomial inversion with a deterministic smoothness allowance. The procedure estimates the counterfactual density from an unaffected bin and covers the entire population identified set uniformly, including zero policy incentives. A likelihood-ratio calculation establishes a finite-parameter Poisson limit for a smooth, known counterfactual submodel. Structural Monte Carlo experiments document both coverage protection and its cost in set length. The results apply to the stated exact-atom observation model; general rounding and optimization frictions require additional assumptions.

title: Zonal-Aware Prostate Cancer Detection and Classification via Hadamard-Fused Mamba-UNet
abstract: Accurate clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) detection from prostate MRI requires a detailed understanding of the prostate anatomical context. Deep learning approaches have achieved promising results in zonal and lesion segmentation; however, the joint analysis of prostate zonal anatomy and lesion morphology in a unified framework remains relatively underexplored. In this work, we propose ZH-Mamba, a multi-stage zonal-aware csPCa detection framework consisting of two H-Mamba UNets models for prostate zonal segmentation and lesion localization, followed by an anatomy-aware Convolutional Neural Network classifier for csPCa detection. The proposed model leverages a learnable Hadamard Transform-based fusion mechanism to enhance zonal and lesion feature representations without increasing computational complexity. The learned fusion patterns consistently emphasize prostate regions, suggesting that the proposed fusion captures anatomically relevant feature representations. We demonstrate a strong zonal segmentation performance on the PI-CAI dataset, reaching Dice scores of $\textbf{0.95}$, $\textbf{0.85}$, and $\textbf{0.95}$ for whole gland (WG), peripheral zone (PZ), and transition zone (TZ), respectively, providing robust anatomical priors for downstream csPCa detection. Experimental results on an independent internal dataset confirm the generalization capability of the proposed zonal segmentation model. For lesion localization, the H-Mamba UNet achieves a competitive Dice score of $\textbf{0.70}$. Integrating the zonal masks and lesion localization, the proposed ZH-Mamba framework achieves an AUC of $\textbf{0.86}$, Average Precision ($\mathrm{AP}_{\mathrm{Patient}}$) of $\textbf{0.72}$, and F1 score of $\textbf{0.76}$, demonstrating the effectiveness of zonal-aware csPCa detection.

title: MetaVul: Agentic Harness Discovery for Vulnerability Detection
abstract: LLM agents are increasingly used to automate vulnerability detection, but reliable detection is challenging because agents must distinguish subtle, security-relevant fixes from benign code variation. While underlying LLM capability has improved significantly, the accuracy of the agent still depends heavily on the harness: the code that defines the scaffolding around the LLM. Harnesses are typically fixed, and largely hand-written, limiting adaptation to evaluator feedback. Additionally, when harnesses are static, improvements on one dataset or model may not transfer to others. To address these challenges, we introduce MetaVul, a self-improving framework for harness discovery in vulnerability detection. Starting from a seed structured reasoning scaffold, MetaVul uses a workflow-based optimization loop to iteratively refine the harness using feedback from paired vulnerable and patched functions, while preserving the structured reasoning and verdict format. At each iteration, it searches over the history of prior harnesses, with access to their trajectories, logs, and metrics, and it returns a set of Pareto-optimal harnesses. We apply MetaVul to discover agent harnesses for various architectures. A validation set (202 pairs) is used for optimization, while an unseen dataset (430 pairs) is kept as the held-out set. We test whether harnesses learned from one model transfer to others not seen during optimization. Results on both frontier and small LLMs show that the optimized harnesses improve pairwise vulnerability detection up to 23.3 percentage points on the validation set and up to 25.8 points on the held-out set with a Pareto-frontier harness. Harnesses learned with one model also transfer to others. We show that harnesses optimized with one model transfer to another, improving held-out pairwise accuracy by 14.7 points without further optimization.

title: LAPIS: Clinically Constrained Patient-Identity Residual Learning for Chest X-Ray Anonymization
abstract: Biometric information in chest radiographs limits their release for research, as patients can be re-identified. We propose LAPIS, which jointly adapts a spatial chest-radiograph latent space so that patient-discriminative information concentrates in a compact, replaceable channel residual while most clinically relevant content stays in the complement. The residual is defined by an exactly semi-orthogonal basis, a spatial adversary suppresses identity leakage from the complement, and replacement-aware training teaches the decoder cross-patient residual swaps under output identity, clinical and realism constraints, so that replacing the residual yields a valid image. At release, the residual is replaced by a mixture of donor residuals. On patient-disjoint model, release and test sets from ChestX-ray14, we evaluate attackers adapted to the anonymized setting, a structural source-retrieval attack, and pathology classifiers trained on released images and tested on real ones. LAPIS reduces worst-case cross-study linkability from 0.961 to 0.791 AUC at a macro AUROC cost of 0.012 relative to reconstruction; a deformation-based baseline, however, remains better at structural source retrieval.

title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
abstract: We study adaptive UAV sampling for radio environment map (REM) construction from non-Gaussian IoT observations. Integrated nested Laplace approximation(INLA) updates a Matérn GMRF posterior, with waypoints selected by entropy pre-screening and Sherman--Morrison lookahead over the reachable set. We show that the likelihood-induced Skew-Normal correction has a sextic entropy effect, explaining its limited influence on waypoint selection. Across 19 retained ray-traced windows,Random and lawnmower sampling cost a median 18.0\% and 14.0\% more residual NMSE than posterior-informed sampling, equivalently reductions of 15.3\% and 12.3\% when referred to those baselines, while differences among informative rules remain unresolved. Widening the prior shadowing standard deviation from 6.0 to 10.025\,dB improves NMSE and credible-interval coverage, with monotone improvement over a 4--16\,dB sweep on this corpus and no observed turning point, although overconfidence persists. Online width estimation from the UAV's own counts yields about 6.5\,dB without recovering the gain. Across 30 measured LoRaWAN propagation windows paired with simulated counts and scored only on received cells, the margin over non-adaptive sampling reproduces, the training-derived width minimizes the tested interval score, and GP-UCB has nominally $3$--$5\%$ lower NMSE. The results show substantial, corpus-dependent sensitivity to prior specification, while fine differences among acquisition rules have limited or unresolved effects, the preferred width depends on the corpus, scored cells and model mismatch.

title: Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne--Ne collisions
abstract: Nucleon-nucleon interactions within atomic nuclei give rise to collective properties such as deformation and nuclear clustering. Ultrarelativistic nucleon-nucleon collisions offer a novel way to probe the many-body correlations of the incoming nuclei, as the nuclear structure is reflected in the initial geometry of the produced system. State-of-the-art low-energy nuclear theory calculations predict highly deformed $^{20}$Ne nuclei with a characteristic $α$+$^{16}$O bowling-pin-like shape. Since such nuclei have recently been collided at the LHC, investigating methods to maximise the sensitivity to the nuclear structure is pertinent. In this paper, we investigate whether body--body and tip--tip configurations of $^{20}$Ne nuclei can be identified in Monte--Carlo Glauber simulations using geometry-sensitive observables: the eccentricity, $\varepsilon_2$, and the transverse compactness, $d_\perp$. The nuclear configurations are obtained from nuclear lattice effective field theory calculations within the framework of Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and $\textit{ab initio}$ Projected Generator Coordinate Method (PGCM). We utilise a Fisher linear discriminant to select body--body and tip--tip configurations based on the $\varepsilon_2$-$d_\perp$ correlation. With classifier thresholds chosen to retain $30\%$ of the target class in a validation sample, the two-variable Fisher selection obtains purities in NLEFT (PGCM) of $0.201$ ($0.156$) and $0.573$ ($0.540$) for body--body and tip--tip events, respectively.

title: Harborth's theorem p(5)=18 revisited
abstract: Let $p(n)$ be the minimum cardinality of a finite planar point set in which each point has exactly $n$ unit-distance neighbours. Harborth proved $p(5)=18$ in work presented in 1985 and published in 1987, using a detailed case analysis. We revisit the proof using convex-hull arguments, incidence counts, and elementary properties of intersections of unit circles. These tools give an alternative treatment of configurations with $14$ and $16$ points and organize the final case distinction by a common vector-sum structure. We also treat a configuration not explicitly covered by the case analysis in the online PDF copy of Harborth's paper available to us, and give an explicit justification of the six-point classification used in the argument. No result subsequent to Harborth's proof is required.

title: Li$^{2}$SAO: Lifting Light Single-Rollout Asynchronous RL Optimization via Group-Relative Actor-Critic Bootstrapping
abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) is becoming a mainstream paradigm for post-training large language models (LLMs), as it improves training efficiency by updating the model as rollouts arrive. Recent work argues that group-wise sampling in GRPO does not naturally fit asynchronous RL training because rollout lengths follow a long-tailed distribution, and proposes Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization (SAO) to improve stability and off-policy behavior, especially on agentic tasks. However, SAO relies on a closed-source value model obtained from scaling value pretraining. In this paper, we analyze GRPO and LiSAO, our lightweight reproduction of SAO without the pretrained value model, on single-turn reasoning and multi-turn agentic tasks. We find that GRPO outperforms LiSAO on reasoning tasks, while the reverse holds on agentic tasks. Since the value model of LiSAO is not yet well trained , LiSAO lags behind GRPO substantially in early training steps. To address this issue, we propose Li$^{2}$SAO, which Lifts Light Single-rollout Asynchronous Optimization with group-relative actor-critic bootstrapping: while the critic is cold, a group-relative advantage trains the actor and a group-centered return trains the critic, after which training switches to single-rollout GAE. Experiments show that Li$^{2}$SAO catches up with or surpasses GRPO in early training and further raises the later performance ceiling. Code is available at https://github.com/jd-cc-coder/Li2SAO.

title: VoxLock: Target-Speaker Extraction for Voice Agents Without an Enrollment Step
abstract: A voice agent's speech recognizer transcribes everyone near the microphone, including people other than the caller. I fine-tuned a public causal target-speaker extraction model (REAL-TSE, 27M parameters) on one GPU to work from a voice sample cut from the call itself, and released it as VoxLock. I score it by what a recognizer writes on real recordings. On Krisp's 265-recording benchmark it reaches 4.95% WER against 23.21% unprocessed and lets 9 background words into the transcript over 85 minutes of background-only speech. Its WER is not significantly different from Krisp's best filters and is significantly lower than the other commercial and open systems I tested. On 400 AMI meeting windows built and frozen before scoring, it cuts WER from 42.95% to 10.63%. The 8-bit model runs a live call on 77% of one CPU thread with 24 ms of algorithmic latency. Model, code and per-file scores are open.

title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
abstract: Medium-voltage feeders have few real-time measurements, so distribution system state estimation (DSSE) rests on pseudo-measurements of the secondary substations, a prior in Bayesian terms. Weighted least squares keeps the power flow exact but reduces this prior to a mean and variance, while supervised deep learning estimators also learn the power flow and are tied to one measurement set. We propose PoSE (posterior sampling for state estimation), which keeps the Bayesian structure of DSSE and learns only what the distribution system operator does not know, namely the distribution of substation injections, modelled by a neural network trained with flow matching on historical data. The power flow equations, grid topology and measurements enter only at sampling, through a noise-aware Kalman-type correction. The neural network therefore never approximates the power flow, but every posterior sample is a physically consistent operating point, and one trained prior serves any measurement set, noise level and topology. On the IEEE 33-bus feeder, PoSE lowers the probabilistic injection error (CRPS) by 6.7-7.5% against a full-covariance Gaussian prior in all 12 tested settings. It provides reliable uncertainty: the 90% intervals contain the true injection almost exactly as often as exact posterior samples would, whereas those of supervised estimators contain it in only 37-78% of cases. On the 240-bus unbalanced three-phase Iowa feeder, it gives the lowest injection, voltage and branch-current errors of all estimators. A fast variant matches this accuracy at 0.2-0.6s per snapshot and, without retraining, beats Gaussian priors and retrained supervised estimators on seven reconfigured topologies.

title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. SKFitter also identifies missing orbital contributions and guide systematic basis set refinement and optimizes parameters through weights. The resulting Hamiltonian can be used to evaluate anomalous (AHC) and spin Hall conductivities (SHC), and topological invariants. We demonstrate the framework using eight representative materials spanning semimetals, semiconductors, transition metals, f-electron compounds, and magnetic systems. Symmetry resolved models achieve band energy errors of 9 to 41 meV within 1 eV of the Fermi level. The fitted Hamiltonians reproduce characteristic features of the SHC response of Pt, the SOC dependence of the AHC of Fe, and the momentum dependent altermagnetic spin splitting of MnTe without any altermagnet specific interaction. For EuMn2Bi2, projection guided orbital refinement reduces the near Fermi level fitting error from 120 to 32 meV. Together, these results establish SKFitter as a flexible and reproducible framework for developing symmetry consistent, physically interpretable TB models of complex materials.

title: On Some Special Cases of the Weber-Schafheitlin Integral
abstract: We consider special cases of the discontinuous Weber--Schafheitlin integral in which the orders $μ$ and $ν$ of the Bessel functions differ by an integer and the exponent $λ$ equals $0$ or $\pm1$, with $μ-ν+λ$ odd. Explicit closed-form results are obtained in terms of Jacobi polynomials.

title: Pareto-Optimal Hypersonic Vehicle Design with Canonical-Coordinate Neural Operator Surrogates Under Ablation-Driven Shape Change and Incidence Variation
abstract: High-fidelity CFD is essential for coupled hypersonic aerodynamic and aerothermal phenomena, but its cost precludes multi-objective design optimization. We develop three DeepONet surrogates for two hypersonic configurations, unified by one device: the trunk receives coordinates in which the varying feature is held fixed. The first is a prescribed family of 37 spherically blunted tangent ogives, varied through ogive radius of curvature to span nose-tip ablation forebody change; no ablation is computed. A body-fitted canonical transformation maps every domain onto a common (s, eta) space, retaining physical coordinates for forces and heat transfer. A branch network predicts reduced coefficients and a Transolver trunk with Physics-Attention learns the spatial basis; a two-step strategy optimizes both jointly, orthonormalizes the basis by QR factorization, and trains a second-stage branch for unseen geometries. Surrogates cover density, pressure, velocity, temperatures, conductivities and species mass fractions. In leave-one-out tests, drag, mean and peak wall heat flux are recovered to 1.16%, 1.62% and 5.29%; a sweep of 1001 geometries gives a 200-design Pareto front trading 6.68% in drag for 4.42% in peak heating (a diagnostic, not an objective). The second is the 3D AEDC waverider at 29 angles of attack: static mesh, moving leading-edge shock. For surface quantities, the same construction predicts integrated heat load within 0.22% and force coefficients to errors below 2.6x10^-5; Pareto fronts identify angles of attack trading drag, lift and heating. For the volume field, a Cartesian trunk smears the shock; a frozen ShockNet supplies a shock-aligned coordinate and a hotspot-aware mixture of experts corrects the residual, recovering density to 12.28% relative L2 error at a held-out incidence (5.08x10^7 nodes). The 1001-design sweep takes about three minutes on a single CPU.

title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) edge pipelines routinely lose contiguous blocks of multi-sensor data to network dropouts and hardware faults. The standard remedy is a disjointed "impute-then-detect" pipeline whose imputer is trained only for Mean Squared Error (MSE). Such an imputer fills a missing block with the most probable normal pattern: a partially observed anomaly is smoothed back toward normality, and boundary artifacts on normal data raise false alarms. We call this imputation bias and propose the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR), a conditional diffusion refiner trained against the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector. Because back-propagating through the sampling trajectory is intractable, the task-aware terms act on the one-step clean-window estimate that the noise prediction already yields, so training costs no more than plain diffusion training. Under strict Point-to-Point evaluation over five seeds with paired significance tests, TADR raises F1 by $0.338$ over the unrefined detector on SMD ($p = 0.0015$), and the anomaly enhancement objective alone contributes $0.463$ in ablation. We also characterise when the method helps: the gain tracks the continuous, mutually redundant channels available and the anomaly evidence the outage removes, and it is absent on telemetry datasets dominated by one-hot command channels and on PSM. At ten sampling steps TADR runs in $41.4$ ms per window on a single CPU core, sustaining about $24$ concurrent 1 Hz streams from a $4.03$ MB model. Code and per-seed results are available at https://github.com/int-park422/TADR.

title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
abstract: Organic molecular emitters are promising building blocks for quantum technologies, but their use at two-dimensional interfaces is limited by diffusion, aggregation, and photobleaching. We present work towards constructing an ultrathin two-dimensional Shpolskii-like host-guest matrix on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by co-depositing terrylene fluorophores with the long-chain tetrapentacontane in a solution-phase process. We demonstrate that this approach disperses terrylene in a roughly one-nanometer-thin alkane layer without detectable phase separation and allows tuning the emitter density from ensembles to isolated emitters showing characteristic blinking behavior consistent with single-molecule fluorescence. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. Encapsulation with hBN from the top side further improves photostability, with emitters demonstrating long lifetimes despite high photon doses. Successful co-adsorption of isolated emitters and alkane matrix is a milestone towards extending Shpolskii-type molecular isolation to hBN and provides a route towards stable, interface-integrated molecular qubits.

title: Model-Agnostic Search for New Physics in the Presence of Imperfect Background by Smearing the Data
abstract: In the search for new particles in high-energy physics, it is necessary to first define the signal region (SR) enriched in signal events, and then compare events in this region with the expected background distribution. While most existing search methods rely on prior domain knowledge of either the signal or the background, there has been less effort to relax both assumptions simultaneously, as methods that weaken one assumption typically rely on strong knowledge of the other. We propose Model-Agnostic Search with Smearing and Imperfect Background (MASSIB), a method that addresses this challenge by learning the density ratio of events relative to a misspecified background distribution using modern tools from machine learning, and defining the SR as the region with high density ratio. Recognizing that a naive application of this idea introduces significant bias in background estimation when interpolating from the control region to the SR, MASSIB mitigates this issue by introducing a "smeared" density ratio, which can be learned efficiently through data-level manipulation and used to define an SR that allows for accurate background estimation. By applying it to various types of simulated Large Hadron Collider (LHC) events with realistic background mismodeling, we demonstrate that MASSIB identifies a data-driven SR that achieves high signal concentration consistently across different types of signals while avoiding bias in background estimation. The method does this without making strong assumptions about either the signal or background distribution. We then show that this robustness extends to the validity and strong statistical power of the resulting hypothesis tests for signal detection, demonstrating the potential of this approach for future model-agnostic searches at the LHC.

title: RiskyPy: Toward Model-Calibrated Prompt Generation for Joint Security and Functionality Evaluation of LLM-Generated Code
abstract: Evaluating approaches that improve the security of LLM code generation requires datasets that jointly assess security and functionality and remain adapted to the capabilities of the models being studied. However, existing benchmarks are costly to produce and are generally not calibrated to a chosen range of model capabilities. We introduce RiskyPy, an automated pipeline that generates security-oriented code-generation datasets calibrated to model proficiency using functionality and vulnerability canaries. We instantiate RiskyPy for Python using domains covering 18 CWEs from the 2025 CWE Top 25, producing 101 prompts. Experiments on Qwen3-4B and Seed-Coder-8B show that the generated tasks remain functionally accessible, with 57-72% of prompts yielding functional code, while only 5-10% of generations are free of Bandit findings, leaving room for joint evaluation of security and functionality of security improvement approaches.

title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
abstract: High dimensionality degrades both the efficiency and the effectiveness of learning algorithms, and in many applications no class labels are available to guide dimensionality reduction. This paper proposes LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID). The method builds on the formal equivalence between LID and the indiscriminability of distance measures. The data matrix is transposed so that each feature is treated as a point, and the LID of each feature is estimated by maximum likelihood from the distances to its $k$ nearest neighboring features. Features with lower LID exhibit greater local discriminability and receive higher importance scores. A refinement step then retains one representative per feature neighborhood and demotes locally redundant features. The result is a complete ranking from which any number of features can be selected without rerunning the procedure. LIDFS does not use any information about labels or the number of classes, and runs in $\mathcal{O}(d^2 n)$ time for $n$ instances and $d$ features. LIDFS is compared with classic and state-of-the-art methods and a random baseline on 23 high-dimensional datasets, the classic benchmark collection. The evaluation uses classification accuracy and AUC with five downstream classifiers, as well as clustering accuracy and normalized mutual information, over both full and aggressive selection ranges. LIDFS ranks first in the supervised evaluations and first or tied second in the clustering-based evaluations. It belongs to the top statistical group together with methods that require the number of classes, and it runs faster than its closest competitor. Several recent methods, by contrast, fail to outperform the random baseline. A sensitivity analysis shows that small neighborhood sizes yield the best results.

title: Thermal Stability and Structural Relaxation Kinetics of Commercially Pure Titanium
abstract: This work explores the structural relaxation of cryorolled commercially pure titanium subjected to subsequent annealing.Nanostructured specimens with an average grain size of ~50 nm were produced by plastic deformation via cryogenic rolling at 100 K to a true strain of 1.20, followed by annealing at 425 K, 525 K, 725 K, and 945 K. Microstructural evolution was examined using electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. Cryogenic rolling was found to induce pronounced grain fragmentation, with coherent scattering regions (CSRs) of 30-50 nm dominating the substructure. X-ray diffraction analysis revealed that annealing drives crystallite growth: a slight increase at 525 K, accelerated coarsening at 725 K, and complete recrystallization at 945 K. The kinetics of grain growth follow the classical Lifshitz-Slyozov-Wagner model, with a growth exponent of ~4, reflecting the role of triple junctions and defect-controlled boundary diffusion. The activation energy, estimated at ~97 kJ/mol, corresponds to typical values for grain boundary diffusion in α-Ti, confirming that cryogenic deformation produces a highly non-equilibrium microstructure whose relaxation is strongly temperature dependent.

title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
abstract: A capable voice assistant must do more than recognize words; it must understand requests, reason over context, sustain conversations, and act through tools. We present Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech-language model that unifies these capabilities within a shared reasoning backbone while retaining text and image input modalities. Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice directly processes speech and generates both responses and tool calls without requiring a separate dialogue model. We introduce a two-stage training procedure to adapt the model to speech. The first stage establishes the speech interface, while the second jointly adapts the projector and backbone through supervised fine-tuning, text replay, and source-dependent cross-entropy and forward Kullback--Leibler divergence supervision. Automatically constructed speech-conditioned dialogues provide conversational training data, while local teacher serving, overlapping teacher and student computation, and fused full-vocabulary losses enable efficient online distillation. In thinking mode, Apriel Voice achieves a score of 98.90 on Big Bench Audio, 81.13 on Speech-BFCL, and a task success rate of 65.51% on $τ$-Voice, with a mean latency of 1.91 seconds. It also achieves 51.27% English EVA accuracy and 74.13% experience pass@1. Finally, we deploy Apriel Voice 27B Preview on a custom serving platform to support interactive voice interactions.

title: Spectral properties of orthorhombic KSbOSiO$_4$ crystals: studies of infrared, visible and ultraviolet radiation absorption, Raman scattering, cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence
abstract: Crystals of orthorhombic KSbOSiO$_4$ (KSS) are often found to synthesize in glass of historical and artistic articles. For instance, these crystallites in the glass of turquoise Bohemian seed beads are known to play a significant role in the process of internal-stress driven corrosion of the glass causing deterioration and destruction of bead embroidered museum exhibits, especially articles made in the early 19th century. In art materials science, KSS has been known since the mid-2010s only for its destructive effects on historical glass objects, but as an optical material it has long been studied. KSS belongs to the group of compounds isomorphic to KTiOPO$_4$ (KTP) and, like other compounds from this group, has anomalies in dielectric constant. The article presents the results of a study of orthorhombic KSS crystals using a number of spectroscopic techniques. IR absorption and diffuse reflection spectra of KSS in the spectral range from 50 to 4000~cm$^{-1}$, its Raman spectrum, its absorption spectrum in the range from near infrared to ultraviolet as well as its cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence spectra are investigated. The constituent peaks of the spectral bands are analyzed and their properties are summarized in tables; the allowed direct and indirect band gaps of KSS are determined. The presented data are necessary both for the correct spectral analysis of historical and artistic glass and enamels, during the production of which this substance was sometimes synthesized in glass, and for a more in-depth study of crystals of the KTP group.

title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
abstract: Continual adaptation requires deciding not only how to update a model, but whether to commit an update without exceeding a declared budget for changes to protected behavior. We introduce Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA), a candidate-agnostic post-update gate that reserves historical observations from candidate optimization, compares old and candidate policies on frozen representations, and selects the largest tested interpolation coefficient whose worst-anchor forward KL divergence remains within budget. The finite check requires neither action labels nor complete trajectories. We develop a theory-led certification framework that separates measured anchor retention from conditional off-anchor guarantees. Under explicit representation-coverage and Lipschitz assumptions, an accepted update satisfies a uniform behavioral-divergence bound on protected support. The analysis gives regularity bounds for affine softmax heads, probabilistic coverage and compression guarantees, interpolation monotonicity conditions, grid-resolution bounds, and trajectory-level and sequential-composition guarantees. In a controlled UCI Human Activity Recognition study used as a non-stationary sensor-policy proxy, CABA reduces mean forgetting from 1.01 percent for unconstrained adaptation to 0.00 percent at budget epsilon = 0.05, while reducing final average accuracy from 93.04 percent to 88.48 percent. The experiment illustrates a retention-plasticity trade-off and does not establish foundation-model or robotic performance. CABA provides an auditable retention check for candidate generators exposing comparable policy distributions and a declared update path, while deployment also requires separate evidence of current-task utility.

title: Likely Metal Scarring in the Magnetic White Dwarf LHS 2534
abstract: There are only three white dwarfs known to possess metal-enriched polar caps due to magnetically guided accretion. These rare systems offer a unique opportunity to study planetesimal accretion and how magnetic fields influence the spreading of material across the atmosphere. To better study these processes however, more targets are needed. Here we report our findings from an observing campaign on the magnetic white dwarf LHS 2534. Time-resolved spectra at the MMT show clear variability in the strength of the Na I and Cr I features. We find that the strengths of these features vary over a period of 19.46 and 19.36 hours respectively, closely matching the 20.22 hour period determined from K2 photometry. Our findings demonstrate the ability to detect and study these variable objects with spectroscopy, and time-series observations of similar targets in the future will provide more insight into how these atmospheres form.

title: Prevented is Not Protected: What Attack Success Rate Hides about RAG
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is vulnerable to knowledge poisoning, where adversaries manipulate retrieved evidence to influence model outputs. Existing defenses are primarily evaluated using attack success rate (ASR), which obscures defense-induced failures and the mechanisms behind apparent attack prevention. To address this issue, this work introduces \textbf{Aligned RAG Evaluation}, a matched-query protocol that jointly examines clean and poisoned responses, with and without defense. By combining matched conditions analysis, LLM-judge endorsement, and retrieval dependence controls, the proposed framework distinguishes prevented from introduced failures, target mentions from LLM endorsement, and single-passage influence from evidence composition. Experiments on HotpotQA and Natural Questions reveal that existing defenses can introduce unexpected target-positive answers, although they can prevent some attacks, while evaluation criteria can also change defense rankings. Our findings expose critical blind spots in ASR-based evaluation and motivate a more comprehensive assessment of RAG poisoning defenses. The code and the evaluation artifact are available at https://github.com/chxhana/aligned-rag-eval.

title: Sharp Nonlocal Poincaré Inequalities and Liminf Lower Bounds for Sobolev and BV Energies on Metric Measure Spaces
abstract: Let $p\in[1,\infty)$, and let $(X,ρ,μ)$ be a complete doubling $q$-Poincaré space for some $q\in[1,p]$ with a lower dimension $d$ and an upper dimension $D$. In this article, we establish Poincaré inequalities for two families of nonlocal nonconvex functionals defined using distances or volumes. More precisely, for any ball $B$ with its radius $r_B\in(0,\operatorname{diam} X)$, any $λ\in(0,\infty)$, and any measurable function $f:X\to\mathbb R$, \begin{align*} &\frac{1}{μ(B)^2}\int_B\int_B|f(x)-f(y)|^p\,dμ(x)\,dμ(y)\\ &\quad\lesssimλ^pr_B^pϕ(B)^{γp}+\frac{λ^pr_B^p}{μ(B)}\mathop{\int_{ΛB}\int_{ΛB}}\limits_{\genfrac{}{}{}{2}{|f(x)-f(y)|}{ρ(x,y)ϕ(x,y)^γ}>λ}\frac{ϕ(x,y)^{γp}}{V(x,y)}\,dμ(x)\,dμ(y), \end{align*} where $V(x,y):=μ(B(x,ρ(x,y)))$ and either $ϕ=ρ$ with $ϕ(B)=r_B$ and $γ\in(-\infty,-\frac{\min\{q,D\}}{p}]$ or $ϕ=V$ with $ϕ(B)=μ(B)$ and $γ\in(-\infty,-\frac{q}{p\max\{q,d\}}]$. Here both ranges of $γ$ are sharp over the class of $q$-Poincaré spaces with the prescribed lower and upper dimensions, and the constant $Λ\in[1,\infty)$ and the implicit positive constant depend only on $p$, $γ$, and the geometric constants of $X$. We also obtain lower bounds for Sobolev energy and total variation in terms of the limit inferior of these functionals, for $γ$ in either the above negative ranges or $(0,\infty)$. Our proofs use the curve characterization of Poincaré spaces and an adaptive dyadic refinement argument based on medians.

title: CLIC: Closed-Loop Intent Consistency for Securing LLM-Driven Control in Open RAN
abstract: With the progressive capabilities of large language models (LLMs), researchers are finding ways to integrate them into the control loops of Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) to enable slicing and resource management through user intents. However, integration of LLMs in the O-RAN control loop via the RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) makes the system vulnerable to \textit{runtime prompt injection threats}, which manipulate control decisions without violating interface authentication, and \textit{residual virtual prompt injection (VPI)} attacks that plant trigger mechanisms to silently steer the behaviour during fine-tuning. Existing studies address only the runtime threat and do not enforce consistency across the full control path, i.e. from the certified A1 intent, through the multi-step LLM trajectory, to the final E2 action. We propose a closed-loop intent-consistency layer (CLIC) that jointly mitigates both threats. The proposed CLIC defines a formal consistency score using a small quantized language model, which is deployed as a Non-RT rApp for model-integrity certification along with a Near-RT xApp for runtime enforcement. We implement CLIC on the OpenAI Cellular (OAIC) platform and evaluate it under domain-adapted JailbreakBench, AdvBench, and VPI workloads. The experimental results show that the proposed CLIC reduces the attack success rate from 0.92 to 0.29 and residual VPI attacks from 0.37 to 0.04, while improving isolation and fairness at slightly higher latency costs, i.e. approximately 27 ms.

title: What It Costs to Trust a Source: A Reproducible Method for Institutional Assessment of Author Disambiguation
abstract: Records of research outputs are curated with care by universities, and the effort is shaped by the external sources from which candidate records are drawn. The curation required before the author identities in such sources can be trusted is examined, and a reproducible method for estimating its cost is set out. Four tests are described; two can be run on public data alone, and two are conducted against an institution's own curated record, taken from Symplectic Elements Discovery portals. The method is demonstrated on OpenAlex and Dimensions across 30 institutions. Of the publications attributed to matched researchers, 50.4\% were confirmed by the institutional record for OpenAlex and 69.6\% for Dimensions, and fewer trusted researcher profiles were retained from OpenAlex at a matched confidence threshold in each of the 30 institutions. Carried through to effort, integrating OpenAlex requires 1.5 times the person-days of review and entry of Dimensions even when each feed is filtered at the threshold that minimises the amount of review required.

title: Homotopy in enriched functor categories: Frobenius exact structures and weak Serre functors
abstract: Let $(\V, \otimes, I,[-,-])$ be a closed symmetric monoidal category with finite (co)limits. Assume that $\V$ is weakly idempotent complete and additive. For a given small $\V$-category $\A$, we investigate sufficient conditions on $\A$ under which the ordinary category $[\A, \V]_0$ of $\V$-functors from $\A$ to $\V$, equipped with the exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$, is a Frobenius exact category,and hence, induces a triangulated stable category. The exact structure $\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}}$ encompasses the degre-wise trivial exact structure on categories of $N$-chain complexes and $m$-periodic chain complexes, with terms in a variety of settings, including left $R$-modules, quasi-coherent sheaves on a scheme, and Banach spaces. We subsequently address the question of describing abstract left and right homotopy relations in $([\A, \V]_0;\mathcal{E}_{\textrm{lowt}})$ in terms of families of morphisms defined objectwise, as in the cases of chain-homotopy and relative homotopy relations. To this end, we introduce the notion of left/right-weak Serre $\V$-functors on $\A$, and investigate their relationships with the classical Serre functor relative to a commutative ring $k$.

title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses
abstract: Effective computer-use agents (CUAs) should seamlessly combine visual GUI interaction with code and terminal execution within a single policy. We present Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4B hybrid CUA trained from a general multimodally aligned checkpoint through an end-to-end, progressive five-stage curriculum across midtraining, SFT, and RL. To power this curriculum at scale, Mage-CUA-Forge replaces per-task agent construction with reusable, skill-conditioned generation workflows and application-specific preparers, synthesizing 293,806 desktop and web tasks across 6,915 skills while reducing recurring per-task expenditure by 82.6%. Rather than directly distilling a default teacher, we evolve the teacher harness and instantiate specialized CUA harnesses to yield high-quality trajectories alongside stage-specific supervision. Mage-VL-Cowork-4B finally climbs to 66.0% on OSWorld-Verified through different training stages with more efficient reasoning cost, achieving state-of-the-art performance at its parameter size and pushing forward the frontier of on-device intelligence.

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Video and Action for Task Generalization in World Action Models
abstract: Achieving the broad task generalization of embodied models in physical environments remains a central challenge in robot learning. We study this challenge in World Action Models (WAMs) through two complementary capabilities: video generalization, which predicts the visual evolution of new tasks, and action generalization, which translates these predictions into executable behavior through a video-to-action bridge. By varying video and action supervision for tasks outside an initial training set, we examine their respective contributions to task transfer. On RoboTwin 2.0, using only in-distribution video-action supervision yields a 25.07% success rate on out-of-distribution tasks. Introducing videos of these tasks without their action labels raises success to 55.90%, while adding just one action-labeled demonstration per task further improves it to 70.70%. These findings suggest that broader video coverage enables task transfer by leveraging existing inverse-dynamics capabilities, while even sparse action supervision further strengthens those capabilities. Guided by this perspective, we introduce WorldBridge, a WAM with separate video and action experts connected through structured attention and trained with joint flow matching. WorldBridge incorporates visual memory at two temporal scales and action forcing, alongside a unified data processing pipeline that standardizes and filters heterogeneous robot trajectories and egocentric hand-derived supervision. Across multiple manipulation benchmarks, WorldBridge achieves state-of-the-art performance among the compared methods, including 96.23% on RoboTwin 2.0 full data setting and 80.9% on clean to random setting, 82.8% on RoboCasa GR1 TableTop, and 57.6% on DOMINO Level-1. Our study highlights the complementary roles of video prediction and action grounding in developing robots that generalize across tasks.

title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
abstract: Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem, since the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. We describe the Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet), a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain of the final state in its architecture. CoReNet builds its event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy, evaluates every jet assignment hypothesis with weights shared across objects, and combines the hypotheses with learned weights using residual networks. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built into the construction, the size of the network does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and the network is trained with the classification loss alone, without generator-level jet assignments. The architecture was developed for the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state and has been used in several CMS searches. On fast-simulation samples of Higgs boson pair production in the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state against QCD multijet production, CoReNet with 1508 trainable parameters performs well above kinematic baselines and trains in minutes on a single GPU. Its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most of the signal events in which it is defined, although no assignment target is used in training. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, the construction carries over to other topologies, which we test with $HH \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-$ against semileptonic $t\bar{t}$. There, encoding the decay chain of the background as well as that of the signal further improves the classification, at a cost of about $10^3$ parameters. In both final states its performance is comparable to that of a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/cms-cmu/CoReNet.

title: Systolic Geometry and Combinatorics of Surfaces
abstract: This thesis investigates two themes. The first studies systolic embeddings of graph on translation surfaces, proving existence results for essential and cellular systolic embeddings and determining extremal genera for certain graph families. The second examines hyperbolic surfaces in the Thurston set, constructing a one-parameter deformation that increases the sys- tole length and produces Bolza-like surfaces, i.e., surfaces whose systolic geodesics decompose the surfaces into triangles, for infinitely many genera. A symmetry property of geodesic inter- sections on these surfaces is also established, together with an application of these Bolza-like surfaces.

title: Safin-1.5: Safety-Native Architecture and Verifiable Reasoning for Recursive Safety Improvement
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) enables large language models to advance their capabilities through successive updates, but these updates can also introduce new risks and weaken existing safeguards. In line with the AI-45° Law, we pursue Safety RSI, in which safety develops as an intrinsic capability alongside general model capabilities through continual risk discovery and repair, while preserving utility and limiting over-refusal. We introduce Safin-1.5, a model built on a safety architecture and trained through recursive safety improvement, with an inference-time harness that extends its capabilities to formal reasoning. Our approach comprises three components: i) The safety architecture combines persistent safety states with hazardous-knowledge disentanglement. The former retains and selectively invokes safety knowledge, while the latter relocates targeted hazardous knowledge into removable experts, enabling its removal with minimal impact on general capabilities. ii) Recursive safety improvement establishes a discovery-evaluation-repair loop. The loop identifies new vulnerabilities and uses experimental feedback to develop repair strategies. It accepts updates only when they improve safety while preserving general capabilities and limiting over-refusal. iii) The formal reasoning harness combines the model's language understanding with symbolic inference and verification. Proof-obligation-guided semantic bridging recovers missing relations in formal representations, enabling symbolic solvers to construct checkable proofs under formalized premises and accepted semantic bridges. Experimental results demonstrate that Safin-1.5 achieves safety and reasoning performance, outperforming frontier models.

title: PathoJev: Efficient Pathology Decisions from Shared Visual Context
abstract: Pathology workflows require multiple visual judgments about the same slide, from identifying tumor type to assessing grade and invasion. Generating and parsing a separate textual response for each structured question adds latency between visual evidence and usable decisions. Building on the System One paradigm, we introduce PathoJev, a pathology model that directly predicts answer probabilities for whole-slide and region-level assessment. PathoJev encodes each slide once and evaluates independent question suffixes in batches over the shared visual context. Reusing the hybrid backbone's recurrent states further limits the computation that grows with slide-context length for each additional question. Across three whole-slide benchmarks, the 9B and 27B models achieve mean accuracies of 77.2% and 78.1%, exceeding SlideChat by 5.4 and 6.3 percentage points. Both scales also maintain competitive accuracy on five ROI benchmarks. On WSI-Bench, the 9B model runs 9.1x faster than SlideChat. Shared context accelerates eight-question workloads by 6.9x and 5.9x over separate prefix encoding, rising to 11.2x and 8.9x for 64 questions. These results provide a reusable probabilistic interface for combining multiple visual judgments in whole-slide and local tissue assessment. Code: https://github.com/ChyaZhang/PathoJev.

title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
abstract: Coding agents increasingly rely on automated approvers to decide whether a proposed shell command may run. Existing approvers, from rule-based checkers to guardrail models and deployed permission classifiers, base their decisions on the text of the request and command. Yet a command's behavior depends on the code it invokes and the state of the workspace, and systems that observe file changes leave the assessment to the agent or a human after execution. We present Caper, a consequence-aware approval mechanism that pre-executes each command in a snapshotted sandbox, provides an independent approver with a bounded report of its observed effects, commits allowed commands, and rolls back blocked ones with a reason the agent can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper achieves the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% versus at least 14.8%) and YoloFS-Ext, a benchmark we build in which harmful behavior is hidden inside invoked tools (7.8% versus at least 35.3%), while blocking 1.0% of the safe twins of the dangerous tasks in YoloFS-Ext.

title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
abstract: While frontier coding agents can generate high-quality 3D scenes and articulated assets, they struggle to create coherent long-horizon animations. When equipped with general-purpose harnesses, they frequently produce physically implausible outputs, generating objects that interpenetrate, lack physical support, or move unnaturally. Such bare agents struggle to repair these errors because they default to scripting the full animation in one pass, making it difficult to verify their work and disentangle complex spatiotemporal constraints. Drawing on the practice of human animators, we introduce DyCraft, a system for animated 3D scene generation that breaks animation into steps that coding agents can more reliably solve. DyCraft first expands the user's prompt into a detailed plan and builds a static scene. It then creates a 3D storyboard of key animation poses, where each frame is a static 3D scene that the agent can build and debug in isolation. Storyboarding decomposes the problem into pairs of verified start and end states, allowing the agent to author local motion between them with a collection of motion authoring tools. We evaluate DyCraft on 24 long-horizon, multi-shot animation tasks covering humanoid robots, human and animal characters, and physical mechanisms. Compared with a native GPT-6 agent in Codex and prior agentic baselines, DyCraft substantially reduces physical violations and generates higher-quality animated 3D scenes that are more often preferred by human raters.

title: Kibble-Zurek dynamics beyond the thermodynamic limit
abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) predicts the universal scaling of topological defect densities generated during continuous phase transitions, a result derived in the thermodynamic limit of homogeneous systems. Yet real materials are intrinsically finite and heterogeneous, raising the question of how nonequilibrium universality survives outside this idealized limit. Here we establish an ensemble-finite-size extension of the KZM that describes critical dynamics in collections of independent finite subsystems with distributed sizes. We test this framework using a polycrystalline model system undergoing a symmetry-breaking transition. We find that the density of topological vortices follows an apparent power law with an exponent approximately half that observed in single crystals. This reduced exponent emerges quantitatively from averaging over the experimentally measured grain-size distribution, without fitting to the measured vortex densities. Our results demonstrate that finite-size effects do not simply suppress KZ scaling but reorganize it into an emergent statistical scaling regime governed by system-size heterogeneity. This establishes microstructure and geometry as control parameters of nonequilibrium critical dynamics and provides a general strategy to engineer scaling behaviour in complex materials.

title: Cavity-engineered ferroelectricity in SrTiO$_3$
abstract: Interfacing quantum materials with photonic cavity architectures is at the vanguard of materials engineering. The structured electromagnetic fluctuations of a dark cavity environment can renormalize fundamental thermodynamical material properties and energy scales, holding promise to create a rich ecosystem of cavity-induced ground states and functionalities absent in the bare material. However, direct experimental demonstrations that cavity coupling can stabilize or enhance genuinely new phases of matter have remained scarce. In this work, we establish the presence of cavity-induced and cavity-enhanced ferroelectric phases in free-standing SrTiO$_3$ membranes coupled to dark THz-frequency photonic crystal cavities. Using THz spectroscopy, we observe ultrastrong coupling (USC) between the ferroelectric soft mode in SrTiO$_3$ and the cavity resonance. The structural response of SrTiO$_3$ to this USC is measured via second harmonic generation imaging, which reveals a substantial (greater than 400%) enhancement of signal in the cavity environment and a distinct modification of the crystalline symmetry, indicating the onset and enhancement of ferroelectricity. We interpret these observations as resulting from renormalized piezoelectric and flexoelectric couplings, which in turn arise from the cavity-modified dielectric environment. This interpretation is supported with microscopic modeling via DFT-based multi-scale dynamics simulations and by macroscopic Ginzburg-Landau theory. Altogether, our experimental and theoretical results firmly confirm that cavity engineering can indeed be used to create new ground states in materials and enhance existing ones. This work establishes a new paradigm for materials engineering with direct applications for quantum transduction, quantum sensing, and nonlinear integrated photonics.

title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
abstract: Humans and animals have a unique capacity to generalize and learn in novel circumstances, including "0-shot" inference (ZI) and continual learning (CL) -- two powerful cognitive abilities. Despite this importance, efforts to model ZI and CL are seriously limited in several ways. First, existing models typically lack components critical to ZI and CL in the brain, namely, strong inductive biases (for ZI) and autonomous control of learning (for CL). Second, models can be less tractable to analysis if model components are overly complex (lacking simplicity), or too task-restricted if model components are overly bespoke (lacking expressivity). Here we introduce autonomous Hebbian networks ("AutoHebb"), a class of online learning feedforward neural networks that realize strong inductive biases and autonomously controlled learning, and are both simple and expressive. Unlike standard models that learn via externally controlled optimization (e.g. gradient descent), AutoHebb networks combine external feedback with internally generated activity to produce a global learning signal ('neuromodulator') fed back to the network. The neuromodulator in turn gates a biologically grounded local learning rule (3-factor Hebbian rule) that updates networks' plastic weights. Using meta-learning to search for fixed (non-plastic) weights, we find that AutoHebb networks (1) succeed on ZI tasks, (2) show emergent (untrained) ZI/CL abilities, (3) admit reverse-engineering into explicit algorithms, and (4) outperform modern learning models on ZI/CL tasks. Lastly, performance comparisons to related models implied an essential role for three model components: meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control of learning. These findings indicate that AutoHebb may be useful in hypothesis generation, analysis, and discovery of biologically grounded forms of learning and generalization.

title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
abstract: Self-evolving agents rewrite a persistent state from feedback, but it is largely untested whether this lets them learn a rule nobody told them. An agent can also pass by writing down each correction as an exception, and its list then grows with every new rule. We introduce CLR-Bench, a Curriculum of Latent Rules benchmark. Each chain adds one hidden rule per level on top of the earlier ones. A rule acts on an opaque label that stands for a named grouping published on the Web, such as the founding members of an airline alliance. The task gives one example value, practice feedback reveals one more member and one non-member, and the test checks unseen members and similar non-members. Probes certify that the base model knows the members of each grouping and does not guess it without feedback, and that the evidence identifies the grouping once labels are read as named groupings. An automated pipeline builds chains from a new data domain, and we release 20 chains over 10 domains. We evaluate six recent self-evolution methods. With the certifying model they barely learn. The best gain at most 5 points over a frozen agent and exclude only 6-12% of the unseen members from the count, fewer than the 20% reached by simply keeping the raw practice history. A fixed lesson that states the named-grouping convention lifts the same methods by 14.5 to 16.5 points. Their states hold the revealed member in 75-98% of cases and almost never the class name, and when practice exposes a member the list misses, they add that member to the list. With the stronger GPT-6-Sol, ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet learn from feedback alone. They reach 78% accuracy and solve 59-60% of the single cells, against 53% and 8% with the certifying model, and they surpass the raw history. CLR-Bench therefore measures how well an agent learns, and this ability differs across models.

title: TAPE: Learning General Audio Effect Representations
abstract: Musicians and mixing engineers often can decipher the signal processing chain they hear on a reference recording, then adapt it to new material. We present TAPE (Transformations of Audio Parameter Embeddings), which estimates this processing from the processed reference audio alone. An encoder trained to identify processors in eight major effect families maps the reference to an embedding. A differentiable digital signal processing (DSP) chain decodes the embedding into editable parameters in one forward pass and applies them to a different unprocessed recording. Its modules are equalization, compression, waveshaping, a small residual network, and reverberation. TAPE achieves lower spectral error than DeepAFx-ST, the previous state of the art for single-step regression, and lower spectral error than per-example search over a chain approximating ST-ITO's, while running 275$\times$ faster than that search. Because the decoder outputs DSP parameters, its chain can also run causally: a C++ implementation with the trained weights processed 128-sample buffers 1.8$\times$ faster than real time, with no missed deadlines.

title: Personalised 3D Mnemonics for Vocabulary Learning in Context
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) can support vocabulary learning by placing mnemonic cues in the physical contexts where new words are encountered. Prior work has augmented real objects with bilingual labels, audio, keywords, and 3D visualisations of those keywords interacting with the objects, but these cues are typically predefined by system designers. This limits scalability and reduces learners' ability to construct personal mnemonic links. By grounding mnemonics in objects that learners already recognise, use, and associate with prior experiences, a system could connect new vocabulary to existing mental models rather than requiring learners to adopt designer-defined associations. We outline a proof of concept and a storyboard of a generative AR approach in which learners create personalised 3D mnemonics by transforming familiar objects in their surroundings into situated mnemonic anchors. We position this concept within a timeline of related work and argue that recent advances in generative 3D asset creation enable a new design point: personalised 3D mnemonics that do not merely place content in the physical learning environment, but modify familiar real-world objects so that they become part of the mnemonic itself.

title: Moiré metals and continuum models beyond a single valley
abstract: We derive continuum models of moiré materials valid over the full monolayer Brillouin zone, as required for metals whose large Fermi surfaces are not confined to a single valley. To this end, we introduce an environment-resolved two-center approximation, in which each hopping amplitude depends not only on the distance between the orbitals it connects but also on its position within the moiré cell. Taking the local environment to be set by the disregistry of the two layers alone, these moiré couplings and their full set of harmonics can be learnt from commensurate bilayers at uniform stackings, without fitting. The method shows excellent agreement with ab initio band structures on moiré cells containing a few hundred atoms. Applied to twisted NbSe$_2$, it yields a continuum model in which moiré effects concentrate at the van Hove singularities, a single-particle starting point for studying moiré-tuned superconducting, charge-density-wave instabilities and their competition.

title: Quantum manifestations of converse symmetry breaking
abstract: Quantum synchronization holds promise in advancing quantum technologies such as sensing, communication, and computation. A key challenge in this rapidly developing field is to identify mechanisms that can promote the emergence of synchronous dynamics. Here, we show that quantum synchronization can be enhanced by introducing controlled heterogeneity in the form of coupling mismatches.
