We carry out this program for finitely many marked copies of the positive Fibonacci category with pairwise nonisomorphic generating simple objects, in the setting of split locally finite semisimple rigid $\CC$-linear tensor categories with simple unit. We show that the Fibonacci fusion relation forces the fusion rules to be those of a specialized Coxeter--Hecke ring. The systems admitting categorification have Coxeter exponents $2,3,\infty$. For every such system we construct a tensor category and prove uniqueness up to marked tensor equivalence. Its simple objects are indexed by the Coxeter group, which may be infinite. Finite rank occurs precisely for disjoint unions of finite ADE diagrams, giving the ADE classification of Fibonacci-generated fusion categories. These categories are unitarizable, with no unitary structure assumed on the candidate. In finite ADE type, allowing Yang--Lee seeds gives one independent tensor-branch choice on each connected component.

title: Wideband Near- and Far-Field Double-Bounce Physical Optics via Co-Area Range Profile Extraction
abstract: Wideband evaluation of the Radar Cross Section (RCS) and the underlying range profile of a target, including its secondary double-bounce fields, remains a computational bottleneck even for modern high-frequency solvers. This paper presents a framework for evaluating the wideband range profile under the Physical Optics (PO) approximation without repeated frequency-domain iterations. Using phase level-set integration via the Co-Area formula, we project the single- and double-bounce scattered fields into frequency-independent Geometric Range Profiles (GRPs), valid in both the far-field and near-field regions. The approach builds on the Radon Transform interpretation of Physical Optics scattering. Unlike point-sampling methods, our discrete implementation bins the profile in range while retaining a complex-valued representation that encodes sub-bin phase corrections, so the field can be evaluated accurately at frequencies well beyond the nominal mesh resolution. We also derive a corresponding time-domain formulation for the scattered transient response to analytic incident pulses. We further show that the classical second-derivative area law for far-field transient scattering extends into the near field as a two-term expression in the derivatives of an isochrone projected area, which reduces to the classical law as the additional induction term decays with range.

title: RECAST: REconstruction of Chain-of-Thought via Auditable Structured Traces
abstract: Large closed-source reasoning models expose only their final answers. The intermediate reasoning that produces those answers is hidden behind API surfaces, tool-call policies, and safety filters. Existing chain-of-thought (CoT) extraction methods assume a side channel: a visible reasoning field, a scratchpad carried through tool calls, or a signed/encrypted reasoning block. We reproduce three representative state-of-the-art extraction methods and find that, on Claude-Sonnet-5.5 accessed through the standard chat-completions interface, all three return zero CoT tokens. The failure is structural rather than a bug: the reasoning field is absent, named tool selection is rejected, free-text scratchpad arguments are filtered, and no replayable reasoning block is exposed. We therefore take a different route. We present RECAST, a reconstruction-based framework that conditions a decoder on the question and the target model's final answer, reconstructs a first-person structured rationale, cleans it, and builds SFT-ready data. To the best of our knowledge, RECAST is the first system to reconstruct CoT from frontier closed models such as Claude-Sonnet-5.5, GPT-6.1, and Gemini 3 without using hidden reasoning channels. We instantiate RECAST on Claude-Sonnet-5.5 and additionally obtain successful qualitative reconstructions on GPT-6.1 and Gemini 3 with the same answer-only protocol. The system is open-source and packaged as an agent skill: one prompt deploys it and runs the complete pipeline to produce SFT-ready CoT data. This preprint describes the system, its threat model, and a controlled artifact validation; it does not claim large-scale benchmark improvements.

title: A Patch is More Than a Token
abstract: Vision Transformers represent each image patch through a canonical token produced under one observation condition. That token is a powerful interface, but it is still one realized state of the patch. We introduce PMTT, which establishes two foundations: a patch representation object can extend from one canonical state to a canonical-centered Representation State Family, and identity-preserving variation opens Patch-Level Local Feature Space. We develop four parts of this representation program. Patch Information Acquisition and Dense Orbital Views expose lawful same-patch states. Visible-to-Hidden prediction tests whether observed states reveal structure beyond themselves. Intrinsic analysis identifies low-dimensional, energy-concentrated, patch-specific, predictive geometry. Representation Organization separates acquiring more information from organizing that information, with an analytic Manifold as the central structured representation. We realize PMTT on frozen DINOv3 S/B/L/H+ backbones without neural post-training of the representation. Across two independent 4,096-anchor cohorts, Manifold explains 70.8-79.6% of Hidden variation, compared with 55.0-72.3% for directly Observed states, and wins on more than 95% of anchors at every scale. Effective rank falls from about 2.5 to 2.0 while dominant energy concentration rises with backbone scale. Across six visual capabilities and four scales, Observed exceeds the canonical Center in 21 of 24 conditions, Manifold exceeds Center in 23, and Manifold exceeds Observed in 16. The strongest current consequence appears in physical correspondence, where MegaDepth satisfies Center < Observed < Manifold at every scale. These results show that pretrained visual backbones contain richer patch information than the standard single-token interface directly exposes. Code and experimental assets are available at https://github.com/zixiongwang-ai/PMTT.

title: Observation-Specific Uncertainty Modeling for Latent-Variable Regression in High-Dimensional Analytical Data
abstract: Across many fields, including medical diagnostics, process monitoring, and quality control, decisions often rely on point predictions for single samples. Observation-specific uncertainty is needed to assess the risk of decision error when predictions are compared with thresholds. Latent-variable regression is widely used for such predictions, but observation-specific uncertainty remains difficult to estimate. Traditional methods assume unbiased predictions, attributing prediction uncertainty solely to variance. However, dimensionality reduction can introduce observation-specific bias, violating this assumption. We introduce a framework using Gaussian processes trained on latent scores and prediction errors to estimate observation-specific bias and error variance, separating systematic error from epistemic and aleatoric variance. In Raman measurements of a fructose-sucrose model system, estimated prediction-error distributions agreed with empirical distributions; bias correction reduced mean squared error, and decision limits incorporating bias and variance improved analyte detection over variance-only limits. An aqueous-solubility application using molecular descriptors demonstrated the framework's generalisation beyond spectroscopy.

title: Fano Resonance of a Magnonic Ring Resonator with a Nano-Scatterer Embedded in a Magnonic Conduit
abstract: We present micromagnetic simulation of a nanoscale magnonic ring resonator coupled to a magnonic waveguide, with and without a hole embedded in the waveguide (H-NRR and NRR respectively), for realizing transformation into a Fano resonance frequency spectral lineshape from a Lorentzian one. Transmission and reflection spectra of the H-NRR and NRR have been analyzed for different structural parameters (embedded hole diameter and gap between the ring and the waveguide) and material parameters (damping factor of the ring) to achieve maximum spectral transmission magnitude variation. The obtained micromagnetic simulation results are supported by an analytical model that consists of two-tracks of wave propagation, forwards and backwards. Our findings show that H-NRR system demonstrates a monotonic dependence of spectral transmission magnitude variation against the aforementioned design parameters (gap and damping) which should provide better engineering controllability and tolerance when compared with the original NRR system. Overall, our proposed structure and study may help in building unconventional magnonic integrated circuits for sensing, data processing systems and computing.

title: Fractional Differential Equations in Chemical Modeling: From Memory and Anomalous Transport to Mathematically Justified Models
abstract: Fractional differential equations are increasingly used to model memory and anomalous transport in chemistry and related fields. However, the formal replacement of an integer-order derivative by a fractional one does not by itself justify fractional dynamics. The essential issue is whether nonlocality can be derived from a physical, stochastic, geometric, or reduction mechanism and whether it leads to experimentally testable consequences. This review, written primarily for mathematicians and specialists in fractional analysis, discusses representative applications in electrochemistry, adsorption and sorption, reaction--subdiffusion, chemical and enzyme kinetics, polymer relaxation, and atmospheric chemistry. Particular attention is paid to distinguishing mechanism-based fractional models from phenomenological fractionalizations. Mathematical questions of well-posedness, nonnegativity, conservation laws, dimensional consistency, parameter identifiability, and numerical convergence are emphasized. Experimental electrochemical examples illustrate the need to distinguish genuine fractional effects from model mismatch or non-identifiability. Several open problems connecting fractional analysis with experimentally grounded chemical modeling are formulated.

title: DIFFNAS: Predictor-Free Neural Architecture Search via Diffusion Model and Zero-Cost Evaluation
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has advanced the automated design of deep networks, but remains computationally expensive due to reliance on model training or performance predictors. We introduce DIFFNAS, a predictor-free NAS framework that leverages a discrete graph diffusion model guided by zero-cost performance proxies. Unlike prior diffusion-based NAS methods that require learned performance predictors, DIFFNAS conditions the generative process on training-free metrics such as MeCo and SWAP, enabling efficient architecture search with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on NAS-Bench-201 show that DIFFNAS finds the optimal architectures for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (94.37% and 73.51%) without a pretrained predictor, while reducing search cost by up to 17.5x compared to DiffusionNAG. On the MobileNetV3 search space, its accuracy is lower than that of DiffusionNAG. These results highlight the promise of diffusion models combined with zero-cost proxies for scalable and effective architecture search.

title: ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers
abstract: Tabular transformer models such as TabPFN achieve strong predictive performance but incur substantial inference costs, making them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained settings. While looped transformers reduce parameter count through weight sharing, they can lose significant predictive power when stopped early. To address this challenge, we introduce the Elastically Looped Tabular Transformer (ElTab), a single model trained to operate across different computational budgets through supervision at randomly sampled early exits. Across 30 OpenML classification datasets, a single ElTab model matches six depth-specific looped models while cutting training cost by more than half, and matches a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs. These results show that elastic-depth training yields a single model that adapts to the deployment budget at hand, offering a favorable trade-off among predictive performance, storage, and computational cost.

title: The Alon-Tarsi number of 4-regular circulant graphs
abstract: This paper studies the Alon-Tarsi number of connected $4$-regular circulant graphs $C_n(s,t)$, where $1\le s<t<n/2$. We prove that if $n=\ell p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $r\ge 1$, and $t\equiv\pm s\pmod{\ell}$, then $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(s,t))=3$ if $\ell$ is even, or if $\ell\ge 3$ is odd and $p\nmid 2^\ell-2$. We also prove that $\operatorname{AT}(C_{6m}(2,3))=3$ for $m\ge 2$, and $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(1,3))=3$ for $n\ge 8$.

title: Compressing the Lawler-Moore Dynamic Program for Weighted Tardy Jobs
abstract: The classic scheduling problem of minimizing the total weight of tardy jobs ($P_m||\sum_jw_jU_j$) asks for a schedule of jobs each with a processing time, weight, and due date on a constant number of parallel identical machines. A job is late in a schedule if it completes after its due date, and an optimal schedule is one where the total weight of all late jobs is minimized. The classic dynamic programming algorithm of Lawler and Moore [Manag. Sci., 1969] solves this problem in $O(nd_{\max}^m)$ where $n$ is the number of jobs, $d_{\max}$ is the maximum due date of any job, and $m$ is the number of identical machines. We show that it is sufficient to only compute part of the dynamic program and obtain the running time $\tilde{O}(n + d_{\max}^{m + 1})$ where $\tilde{O}$ suppresses polylogarithmic factors. This affirmatively answers the open question posed by Hermelin, Molter, and Shabtay [INFORMS J. Comput., 2024], whether a running time of $\tilde{O}(n + d_{\max}^2)$ is possible on a single machine.

title: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
abstract: Vector Quantization (VQ) is a rapidly evolving technique for compressing Large Language Model (LLM) weights, reducing memory usage, and speeding up inference. However, extreme compression deteriorates model performance, which is challenging to recover due to the discrete nature of VQ parameters. Existing methods employ training-free approaches that are limited to layer-wise reconstruction loss minimization. To address this limitation, we propose TVQ, a novel method that leverages straight-through estimation to enable gradient descent-based optimization of vector-quantized LLMs. By reformulating VQ LLM optimization with trainable latent weights, TVQ enables arbitrary objective minimization. We constitute our approach by applying TVQ in a block-wise knowledge distillation paradigm, which balances quality and training efficiency, and propose several practical solutions to accelerate training. In experiments on modern LLMs, we demonstrate that TVQ is compatible with modern VQ schemes. As a result, TVQ achieves state-of-the-art quality in low-bit post-training quantization settings with a modest training budget and straightforward PyTorch implementation. For instance, TVQ achieves near-lossless 2-bit quantization for LLaMA2-70B with only 1% accuracy drop on popular Question-Answering benchmarks.

title: Primordial black holes and gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation
abstract: We study the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) in aligned axion inflation through the transition between two stages of inflation. The first stage proceeds along a metastable trajectory and ends when this trajectory loses stability, causing the fields to turn towards the attractor of the second inflationary stage. During the transition, coupled adiabatic--entropy evolution produces a localized enhancement of the curvature power spectrum. We compute the PBH abundance from this spectrum assuming Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations and using the nonlinear compaction-function formalism with a spectrum-dependent collapse threshold and critical collapse. Representative benchmark solutions yield asteroid-mass PBHs with a potentially significant dark-matter abundance, together with an associated SIGW background.

title: Overcoming the Representational Limitations of Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks
abstract: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) offer a framework for learning functions from classical data, but their expressive power depends critically on how inputs are encoded into quantum states. Angle encoding can require resources that scale with the number of features, whereas amplitude encoding represents $d$ features using only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2 d)$ qubits. This compactness comes at a representational cost: normalization makes conventional amplitude encoding invariant to nonzero real rescaling of the input, up to an unobservable global phase. We show that this invariance induces an exact, architecture-independent restriction on the resulting hypothesis class. No downstream quantum circuit can distinguish inputs differing by nonzero real scaling. We develop a general condition under which deterministic preprocessing can remove this ambiguity and show that nonlinearity alone is insufficient. Based on this analysis, we introduce a fixed nonlinear feature map that provably distinguishes all real inputs under subsequent amplitude encoding, without adding trainable parameters and while retaining logarithmic qubit scaling. We evaluate the resulting QNN on three canonical classification benchmarks and a nonlinear synthetic dataset against conventional amplitude and angle encoding, as well as a classical neural network. Across these tasks, the proposed encoding consistently improves classification accuracy over both quantum encoding baselines by 21$-$44 %. Our results establish normalization-induced scale invariance as a concrete representational bottleneck of amplitude encoding and demonstrate that it can be removed while preserving a compact quantum representation, marking a step toward quantum models capable of capturing arbitrary relationships in classical data.

title: Where KV-Cache Error Lives in Looped Language Models: A Diagnostic Study of Ouro and Huginn
abstract: A looped language model applies one block of layers 4 times per token and keeps a key/value (KV) plane for each loop. We study where storage error changes the next-token distribution and how shared-weight error accumulates, using Ouro-1.4B (4 loops) on GSM8K and MATH and Huginn-0125 (32 loops) on GSM8K-derived chains, with dense, simulated quantization. Per unit of error, values carry 94% of the diagonal Fisher mass, but measured KL is dominated by keys with larger quantization errors. Local second-order prediction follows the measured KL of typical sequences, including 136 held-out chains, but misses a few confident rows, and a local second-order factor for shared weights at 32 loops ranges from 1.65 (INT8) to 4.09 (INT4), so it depends on the error direction. A cell-level allocator lowers one-step KL at 25-48% of BF16 bytes, while paired task-accuracy comparisons depend on budget and the 25% gap against K4V2 shrinks to near zero under a post hoc answer-extraction check. A later Ouro-2.6B test retains the key/value split but falsifies measured-cost allocation's advantage over Fisher at 31%; across all 21 ledger registrations, 60 of 176 criteria failed.

title: Switching off a high-harmonic polarization channel by anti-unitary symmetry
abstract: We study polarization-resolved high-harmonic generation in a laser-driven two-leg Su--Schrieffer--Heeger ladder with asymmetric dimerization under periodic boundary conditions. A field linearly polarized along the ladder can generate both longitudinal and transverse radiation, whose harmonic content is controlled by lattice symmetry and electronic filling. Using symmetry analysis of the time-dependent density matrix, we show that reflection symmetry enforces odd-order harmonics in the longitudinal response and, when the transverse response is nonzero, even-order harmonics in the transverse direction. At half filling, an additional anti-unitary symmetry relating the occupied and empty bands suppresses the transverse current completely. A unitary chiral symmetry in the clean ladder relates the same bands but fails to enforce this cancellation, showing that band swapping alone is insufficient: the suppression requires both a density-matrix constraint that persists during the driven evolution and the appropriate transformation of the transverse-current operator. Moving away from half filling lifts this cancellation and allows transverse emission, while the reflection selection rule remains whenever reflection symmetry is preserved. Numerical calculations at quarter and half filling, combined with onsite potentials that selectively break the relevant symmetries, confirm these two distinct mechanisms. Thus, reflection symmetry determines which harmonic orders occur, whereas the interplay of anti-unitary symmetry and filling controls whether the transverse HHG channel is present at all.

title: Creating functional nanostructures for vortex manipulation in superconducting Bi$_\text{2}$Sr$_\text{2}$CaCu$_\text{2}$O$_\text{8+x}$ thin films via focused He ion beam irradiation
abstract: Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+x}$ (Bi-2212) is a highly anisotropic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting unique vortex dynamics due to its layered structure. Precise nanoscale patterning of ultrathin Bi-2212 films remains challenging, limiting controlled studies of vortex pinning. Here, we employ 30 keV focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation to fabricate periodic arrays of columnar defects with 100 nm spacings in optimally-doped Bi-2212 thin films, thereby creating artificial vortex pinning centers. Magnetotransport measurements reveal pronounced vortex matching effects, evidenced by minima in magnetoresistance and peaks in critical current at commensurate magnetic fields. The angular dependence of magnetoresistance and critical current scale with an effective magnetic field, indicating strong confinement of pancake vortices along irradiation-induced tracks. These findings demonstrate the efficacy of He-FIB nanopatterning in modulating the superconducting properties in Bi-2212 thin films, providing a platform for fundamental studies of vortex matter and advancing prospects for device applications based on this highly anisotropic superconductor.

title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians
abstract: Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $γ$ with a $K$-orbit $κ$, and $M=κ\capγ$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $γ$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $κ$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.

title: Decomposing super unitary representations using Berezin integration
abstract: I introduce the notion of a family of super unitary representations depending upon odd parameters as well as the notion of a direct Berezin integral of such representations. I use this to decompose the (left-)regular representation of the super Heisenberg group and of a super Heisenberg-like group into smaller (irreducible) subrepresentations. I compare the obtained subrepresentations to the representations obtained by applying (super) geometric quantization of the coadjoint orbits of the corresponding groups. It turns out that for the super Heisenberg group we need coadjoint orbits with an odd symplectic form in order to describe all subrepresentations found in the decomposition and for the Heisenberg-like super group we even need orbits with a non-homogeneous symplectic form.

title: Resonant Amplification of Demographic Noise in Stochastic Common-Pool Resource Dynamics
abstract: Common-pool resources are vulnerable to overexploitation, yet many social-ecological systems exhibit persistent oscillations. We introduce a stochastic eco-evolutionary model in which harvesting strategies and resource availability shape one another. In the infinite population limit the system approaches a stable state through damped oscillations. Demographic noise continually excites these modes, generating instead robust macroscopic quasi-cycles, whose frequencies depend on the noise ratio, the relative timescale between strategy and resource, and the harvesting pressure. The model reproduces the distinct frequency peaks, observed in empirical global fish-landings data for high- and low-income countries, showing that persistent environmental fluctuations can emerge naturally from demographic noise.

title: Toward Quantum Monte Carlo for Sovereign Debt Risk: A proof of concept
abstract: We present a proof-of-concept pipeline that applies quantum amplitude estimation to the probability that a sovereign debt-to-GDP ratio exceeds a critical threshold at a given horizon. The pipeline combines a reduced two-factor Gaussian debt model linearized around its mean, quantum state preparation on a 32 x 32 grid, a weighted-adder circuit, an integer comparator, and Maximum Likelihood Amplitude Estimation (MLAE). On a noiseless statevector simulator with 500 shots per Grover power, the circuit estimate (a = 0.1152) agrees with the circuit's exact target amplitude (0.1153), and the observed estimation error is consistent with the amplitude-estimation scaling in the number of oracle calls. The model used here is deliberately simple: it admits a closed-form solution, so the contribution is a demonstration of the encoding and estimation workflow, not a practical advantage over classical methods. We discuss the conditions under which such a pipeline could become relevant and the obstacles that remain.

title: Pareto climate economics: optimism, pessimism and the polarization of societies
abstract: We argue that simple conceptual models of the relation between short-term efforts in climate mitigation and adaptation policies (STECM&AP) and possible climate damages can help understanding the difficulties of increasing public support for a transition towards sustainable, decarbonized economies. Specifically, we show that, under fairly general conditions, mistrust and pessimism tend to polarize support for either minimal ``business as usual'' policies or maximal ``all-in climate mitigation efforts'' choices. Under the same conditions, trust and optimism tend to de-polarize societies towards moderate climate mitigation and adaptation (CM&A) policies and promote social consensus. If the relation between short-term efforts and possible climate damages can be quantified via empirical or model data, Pareto climate economics can be applied to extend these conceptual models and support climate decision making with trustable computational methods.

title: PGGT-Loc: Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer for Feed-Forward Camera Localization
abstract: Camera localization methods are mostly multi-stage pipelines relying on dedicated and complex maps that are costly to construct, store, and maintain over time. Alternatively, well-structured maps that organize scenes with compact yet expressive primitives are often readily available, providing rich structural and semantic cues that humans can interpret. However, their potential for direct camera localization remains largely unexplored due to the significant modality gap between map primitives and visual observations. This motivates a new concept for localization, which estimates camera poses by grounding query observations to map primitives. In this paper, we instantiate the concept in the context of planar primitives with PGGT, the Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer network. Given a single query image and a set of planar map primitives, the network is trained to predict multiple localization targets for feed-forward 6-DoF camera localization that generalizes to unseen environments. With this straightforward and scalable architecture, our method pushes the state-of-the-art localization performance on both dense surface maps and minimal layout models. The code and models are available at https://github.com/3dv-casia/PGGT-Loc

title: ObjectGuidedMap: An Object-Aware Model for Robust Bird's Eye View Map Prediction in High-Occlusion Scenarios
abstract: Accurate BEV map prediction is a critical component of autonomous driving systems, enabling downstream planning and control. Recent approaches such as Mask2Map achieve strong performance by predicting vectorized, instance-level map elements directly from multi-view images. However, existing BEV map prediction models operate largely independently of object-level scene understanding, despite the fact that traffic participants frequently occlude or implicitly encode information about road geometry. In this work, we propose a multitask architecture that jointly predicts BEV maps and 3D objects, explicitly enabling information exchange between the two tasks. Building upon Mask2Map, we introduce an object detection branch and incorporate cross-task feature fusion at both the BEV feature level and the instance-query level via deformable attention and cross-attention mechanisms. This design allows map instances to leverage object context while remaining robust to occlusions caused by traffic participants. Experimental results on the nuScenes and Argoverse 2 datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently improves BEV map prediction accuracy, with particularly significant gains of 21% mAP in scenes containing heavy object occlusion.

title: ReuScope: Auditing Data Reuse and Evaluation Sensitivity in Capsule Vision 2024
abstract: We develop ReuScope, a protocol for auditing data reuse and evaluation sensitivity, using Capsule Vision 2024 as a case study. It combines measurements of data relationships with two comparisons: changing the evaluation population while holding predictions fixed, and changing training data while holding evaluation fixed. Byte-identical files cross the public training-validation boundary, and all 41 Kvasir-Capsule recordings that contribute frames occur in both partitions. Shared source recordings establish cross-split overlap; missing cross-recording patient identifiers prevent counting unique shared patients. Across ten paired seeds, removing all training rows attributed to Kvasir-Capsule, plus five rows from other sources flagged as near-matches to it, lowers public-validation balanced accuracy from 82.5% to 61.2%. Evaluating the same fitted models on the validation rows of the other sources reverses the comparison: removal improves balanced accuracy by 1.38 percentage points. The public-validation drop measures sensitivity to source removal, not an amount of leakage-induced inflation. Matched controls show that sample size and class counts alone do not explain the observed score differences. An exploratory experiment removes the training neighbors of validation frames that have close training matches, or equally many distant training rows, and yields a difference-in-differences estimate, relative to matched unflagged frames, of -0.355 percentage points in true-class probability; the paired-t interval for accuracy spans zero. The resulting procedure distinguishes observed reuse from conditional performance sensitivity and specifies the population, class support and uncertainty unit for each conclusion.

title: 6G-Enabled Cooperative Connected and Automated Mobility: Are We There Yet?
abstract: Connected, cooperative, and automated mobility (CCAM) is a key enabler of future intelligent transportation systems, requiring seamless integration of communication, sensing, computing, and automation technologies. This paper surveys the state of the art in CCAM, focusing on key use cases and performance indicators, enabling technologies, system architectures, and standardization and regulatory developments relevant to large-scale deployment. Particular attention is given to cooperative perception, collective awareness, artificial intelligence and machine learning as fundamental building blocks of future CCAM ecosystems. The paper further identifies major research challenges related to scalability, interoperability, and real-time operation in highly dynamic mobile environments. Finally, it outlines future research directions toward achieving large-scale, safe, and resilient CCAM systems supported by next-generation communication networks.

title: A Deterministic Commitment Rule over Unstructured DAGs for Optimistic Replication
abstract: In optimistic replication protocols, each replica uses the local state to execute requests from its clients in a wait-free manner, without synchronizing with other replicas. The outcomes may be revised later, making optimistic protocols only eventually consistent. To compensate for this consistency loss, an additional commitment mechanism can be employed: an underlying atomic broadcast protocol that allows replicas to periodically agree on the evolution of the object state. In this paper, we introduce a simple framework for optimistic replication based on a causality DAG: every replica represents the object state via a causally ordered set of client operations. The framework incorporates a deterministic commitment rule that incurs virtually zero message overhead beyond the basic dissemination of submitted operations.

title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. The full-potential treatment also recovers the semiconducting character of Si. Further calculations for elemental Ge and Sn establish the applicability of the approach across group-IV materials. Extending this framework to SiGeSn alloys, we investigate their composition-dependent equilibrium lattice parameters, bulk moduli, and mixing enthalpies. The calculated lattice parameters exhibit positive deviations from Vegard's law, while the bulk modulus decreases substantially with changes in alloy composition. Moreover, positive mixing enthalpies of 180.92 and 346.32 meV/atom are obtained for Si0.5Ge0.375Sn0.125 and Si0.375Ge0.25Sn0.375, respectively, indicating an energetic penalty for homogeneous alloy formation relative to the selected elemental reference states. These findings highlight the importance of nonspherical potential contributions in accurately describing open-structured semiconductors and establish KKR-FP within MuST as a promising framework for investigating the structural properties and mixing energetics of compositionally complex group-IV alloys

title: Integrating Low-Thrust Transfer Dynamics into POMDP Planning for On-Orbit Servicing
abstract: Recent developments in both high-thrust (HT) and low-thrust (LT) propulsion technologies broaden design options for on-orbit servicing (OOS) missions. However, incorporating LT transfers into OOS mission planning requires accounting for the trade-off between prescribed transfer duration and propellant consumption. Multi-servicing, multi-transfer OOS mission planning is inherently sequential and requires adaptive planning tools that account for propulsion-dependent transfer durations and mass-dependent propellant consumption. Thus, transfer dynamics must be integrated into mission planning and scheduling to increase flexibility and adaptability. In addition, the planning is often done with imperfect information about the system's state and stochastic service demands. This paper focuses on modeling orbital transfers, particularly LT transfers, within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) framework for OOS mission planning. To enable offline policy computation, the transfer model must provide explicit state transitions and rewards for all admissible actions. The state space is therefore augmented with the servicing vehicle's remaining propellant to enable consistent mass updates. HT transfers are modeled using a precomputed transfer matrix that maps each transfer to the time of flight and propellant consumed. LT transfers are represented using an analytical GEO phasing model with prescribed transfer-duration alternatives. For each alternative, the model calculates propellant consumption and maneuver feasibility as functions of the required phase change and the current servicing-vehicle mass. The proposed modeling approach is evaluated on simplified OOS planning scenarios using circular phasing with HT and LT propulsion. The resulting POMDPs are solved using the Successive Approximations of the Reachable Space under Optimal Policies (SARSOP) algorithm, and the policies obtained under HT and LT are compared. This comparison provides a quantitative assessment of the feasibility and operational impact of LT options, particularly regarding the potential role of advanced electric propulsion in future servicing architectures.

title: Revisiting the directed pathwidth of h-semicomplete digraphs
abstract: A digraph is $h$-semicomplete if every vertex has at most $h$ non-neighbors. In semicomplete digraphs, $k$-triples are obstructions to bounded directed pathwidth with many algorithmic applications: Fradkin and Seymour [JCTB 2013] showed that a large triple contains a subdivision of every small digraph, and triples were used for irrelevant vertex arguments in routing problems by Fomin and Pilipczuk [JCTB 2019] and Gomes, Lopes, and Sau [ICALP 2025]. Fradkin and Seymour also showed that there is a function $f(k)$ such that every semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth at least $f(k)$ contains a $k$-triple, and their proof gives $f(k)$ triply exponential in $k$. For $h$-semicomplete digraphs, a result of Kitsunai et al. [ESA 2015] also yields a $k$-triple, but only existentially, and finding one in fixed-parameter time remained open. We improve the bound on $f(k)$ to a single exponential and extend the result to $h$-semicomplete digraphs: we show that every $h$-semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth greater than $(h+1) \cdot k \cdot 2^{27k+9}$ contains a $k$-triple, which we find in polynomial time, and no bound subexponential in $k$ or sublinear in $h$ is possible. We also extend the approximation algorithm for directed pathwidth of Fomin and Pilipczuk to $h$-semicomplete digraphs, so its certificates of large directed pathwidth remain valid. Our proof is much shorter than the analysis of Kitsunai et al., and while their algorithm is exact, ours runs in polynomial time. As an application, we show that Arc-Disjoint Paths on $h$-semicomplete digraphs is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of paths and $h$, generalizing the semicomplete case. Finally, unlike in semicomplete digraphs, directed pathwidth does not bound directed cliquewidth: for every $k$, some acyclic $1$-semicomplete digraph, so of directed pathwidth zero, has directed cliquewidth at least $k$.

title: Open-Weight MLLMs Cannot Compare What They Cannot Name
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly capable of understanding images and performing complex visual reasoning, suggesting the possibility of using them to automate biological image analysis. This need is becoming increasingly urgent as advances in technology continue to generate ever larger and more diverse microscopy datasets, already exceeding the scale at which manual visual analysis is feasible. With the final aim to use MLLMs for visual comparison of complex phenotypes, we investigate a very simple baseline: comparison of the size of body parts in synthetic images of ants. We find that state-of-the-art open-weight MLLMs fail for some body parts, but not for others, even though the comparison itself is visually trivial for all of them. We evaluate different in-context learning strategies and analyze performance on the related object recognition task. Our results suggest a recognition-driven grounding failure: structures that the models cannot recognize are instead associated with a recognizable semantic concept, impairing the grounding and comparison of both. Further analysis of the vision encoder is consistent with the hypothesis that fine-grained visual structure may be less well preserved without semantic support. Together, our results reveal a surprising limitation of current MLLMs: semantic recognition can gate simple visual comparisons that do not intrinsically require semantic understanding. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/kreshuklab/Open-Weight-MLLMs-Cannot-Compare-What-They-Cannot-Name

title: The multiple origins of spurs in stellar streams: a challenge for dark matter diagnostics
abstract: Spurs along stellar streams are often interpreted as signatures of interactions with dark matter subhalos, and thus have been proposed as diagnostics on the clustering and nature of dark matter. Although galactic baryonic components could play similar roles as gravitational perturbers of streams, the possible signatures they leave and the degeneracy with subhalos have been overlooked. In this paper, we analyse simulations of streams experiencing disruptions by dark matter subhalos, a galactic bar, and a galaxy merger. Although spurs are more frequently found to be induced by the galaxy merger, the spurs originating from all these processes are morphologically similar. Therefore, such morphological features should not be used alone to characterise the mechanism of their origin, nor to constrain the nature of dark matter.

title: A conjecture on Galois groups and large fields
abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $K$ be a field such that $p$ is prime to the absolute Galois group $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$, in the sense that $p$ does not divide the degree of any finite Galois extension of $K$. We conjecture that $K$ is large in the sense of Pop: any smooth algebraic curve $C$ over $K$ with a $K$-rational point has infinitely many $K$-rational points. This conjecture would have some consequences in mathematical logic. For instance, it would imply the expected classification of stable fields of positive characteristic. We give some weak evidence for this conjecture. Specifically, suppose that $K$ is a perfect field and $\operatorname{Gal}(K)$ is prime to $p$. Then every abelian variety $A$ over $K$ has Zariski dense $K$-rational points, and if $C$ is a smooth curve of genus less than $7-p$ with at least one $K$-rational point, then $C$ has infinitely many $K$-rational points.

title: SketchMate: Agentic Geometric Reasoning for Zero-Shot Precision Insertion
abstract: Inserting an unseen part requires sub-millimetre precision and the correct orientation of keyed features. Current zero-shot agentic manipulation methods built on vision-language models (VLMs) produce spatial outputs that are far too coarse for this. We propose to let a VLM build a sketch model of the task, i.e., a few geometric primitives and two mate frames, which a VLM agent measures with geometric tools in multi-view depth and which a standard planner and compliant controller execute. Because a sketch describes the parts independently of their placement, the robot needs to build it only once per task. A sketch memory stores each agent run and transfers the stored sketch to later placements by point-cloud registration, so that the VLM is called only for unfamiliar parts. After grasping the part, the robot inspects both mating faces at close range and corrects the sketch by shape matching. On 69 simulated insertion episodes, our method inserts 88% of the parts at the assembled pose in a strict kinematic test, while ReKep and MOKA with the same VLM insert none. On new placements of eight tasks, reusing one stored run inserts as many parts as calling the agent in each episode, and it produces the sketch in 3.4 s instead of about 90 s.

title: Area laws for free fermions in ergodic field: spectral criteria and localisation-based methods
abstract: We review rigorous results concerning the Area Law for the entanglement entropy of free fermions whose one-body Hamiltonian is an ergodic Schrödinger operator with a strongly localised pure point spectrum. Particular attention is paid to operators with deterministic potentials (quasi-periodic ones and those generated by subshifts of finite type). Our approach relies on reducing the problem to obtaining exponential estimates for the eigenfunction correlator. This provides an effective route from localisation to the Area Law and allows for the identification of additional spectral estimates that need to be proven for various classes of ergodic operators. We realise this approach by using various localisation techniques, including dynamical localisation and the uniformly localised eigenfunction property for bounded and unbounded ergodic operators (e.g. the Maryland model), as well as a new method for obtaining the corresponding exponential bounds for Schrödinger operators generated by subshifts of finite type.

title: A multi-wavelength view of PSR J0437-4715 with NICER and other missions: Radius measurements from far-ultraviolet to hard X-ray pulse profile modeling
abstract: We report updated mass and radius measurements for the millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 obtained with pulse profile modeling of the emission from the far-ultraviolet to the hard X-rays. Using an extended 2.56 Ms Neutron Star Interior Composition ExploreR (NICER) dataset together with XMM-Newton, Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope ARray and Hubble Space Telescope observations, we perform Bayesian inference with models describing the thermal emission from hot spots of increasing complexities, together with the rest of the warm NS surface, as well as the non-thermal emission component represented by a phase-dependent (pulsed) power-law. With this comprehensive model and broadband data set, as well as radio timing priors on the mass, distance and inclination, our headline result for PSR J0437-4715 led to a mass M = 1.377(-0.034)(+0.038) Msun and an equatorial radius Req = 11.35(-0.39)(+0.40) km, one of the narrowest measurements of Req from NICER observations of millisecond pulsars. The geometric configuration favors a non-antipodal hot spot distribution, as noted in previous analyses of this pulsar. When combined with recent measurements of M and Req of other pulsars, the tight constraints from PSR J0437-4715 further reduce the allowed range of the dense matter equation of state, excluding those that predict radii above 12.0 km (at the 68% level) for all NS masses.

title: Bar likelihood in local galaxies: the joint role of stellar mass, morphology and environment
abstract: We investigate how the likelihood of hosting a stellar bar depends on both intrinsic galaxy properties and environment, using a volume-limited sample of central and satellite galaxies from the NASA-Sloan Atlas, spanning isolated systems, low- and high-richness groups, and massive haloes, complemented with halo-based environmental information and probabilistic morphology. Using probabilistic bar identification, we quantify the bar likelihood as a function of stellar mass, colour, morphology, halo mass, and cluster-centric distance. We find that stellar mass and morphology are the galaxy properties most associated with the bar likelihood. At fixed morphology, the probability of hosting a bar increases with stellar mass, particularly for late-type galaxies. At the same time, morphology strongly modulates the overall incidence of bars, with early-type galaxies displaying systematically lower probabilities than late-type systems across the stellar mass range. Environmental trends are observed, including halo mass and cluster-centric distance, but these trends largely reflect the morphological composition of the galaxy population. In particular, the decrease in bar likelihood towards the centres of massive haloes reflects the increasing fraction of early-type galaxies, consistent with the morphology-density relation, rather than a direct environmental suppression of bars. Our residual analysis finds no statistically significant residual dependence on halo mass or normalized cluster-centric distance after accounting for stellar mass and morphology, within the sensitivity of this sample. Overall, our results show that stellar mass and morphology are the main factors associated with bar likelihood.

title: Engineered Learning Problems on Noisy Quantum Processors
abstract: Despite quantum machine learning being an active topic of research, demonstrations of algorithms run on quantum hardware beating classical methods remain rare. In this work, we demonstrate a significant performance gap using a projected quantum kernel for $n=15,30$ and $45$ qubits over classical methods on an engineered classification problem, and show reproducibility of the results over different quantum processor units. We also demonstrate how error mitigation can widen this gap, both by improving hardware performance but also by increasing the classical difficulty, with different techniques contributing unequally to these phenomena. This work provides strong evidence that superior empirical performance of quantum hardware over all classical techniques is an achievable goal in quantum machine learning, albeit for an artificial problem. However, as with any application relying on observables, beating state-of-the-art simulation methods remains the primary challenge, as our matrix product state results here show.

title: Improved estimation of differential entropy of a multivariate Gaussian distribution
abstract: We consider estimation of entropy of a multivariate variate normal distribution with unknown mean vector and unknown covariance matrix. Using a decision-theoretic approach, we study the problem under a general location-invariant loss function that is strictly convex and minimized at zero. We first characterize the class of affine equivariant estimators and obtain the best affine equivariant estimator. We further show that the best affine equivariant estimator is inadmissible under the general loss. Exploiting information in the sample mean, we derive Stein-type improved estimators, including an extension to the case of a mean matrix. Under the linex loss, we obtain a smooth Brewster--Zidek-type estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator, and we show that this estimator is generalized Bayes under a suitable non-informative prior.

title: Dynamical Memory Transformer: Selective Recurrent Memories with Constant Cost Attention
abstract: Transformers retain an explicit history of the sequence, allowing attention to directly retrieve past representations. However, the size of the KV-Cache and the cost of a new token increase with the context length. State Space Models compress the past into a fixed-size recurrent state, at the cost of reduced addressability. We present the Dynamical Memory Transformer (DMT), a hybrid architecture that separates sequence encoding from information reading. The encoder uses several memory units, each implemented by a dynamical system with a complex diagonal recurrent matrix. An input-dependent leak rate controls their updates. The decoder then uses attention to read and combine their outputs, without going through the token history. The formulation of the recurrence allows an associative scan with O(T ) total work and O(log T ) parallel depth, with fixed dimensions. During autoregressive inference, the recurrent states and the convolution cache remain fixed in size. We compare DMT with Mamba and Transformer on cognitive and language modeling tasks, and show its strengths and limitations: DMT achieves the best results on several cognitive tasks and language modeling performance close to that of Transformer, but remains behind Mamba in language modeling. On selective copy, DMT also shows stronger length extrapolation than Mamba and Transformer. These results demonstrate that parallel dynamical memory units are a promising mechanism for retaining and using information over sequences.

title: Magnetic control of reflectionless states and an intrinsic-mode exceptional point in a magnon-phonon coupling system
abstract: Reflectionless states (RLs) and exceptional points (EPs) are hallmark singular responses of non-Hermitian systems, with potential applications in sensing, wave control, and energy manipulation. Yet, realizing and independently tuning these states in a compact integrated platform remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate two-dimensional magnetic control of RLs and EPs in an on-chip magnon-phonon system based on a FeGaB-32 degree-YX-LiNbO3 heterostructure. The magnetic-field magnitude tunes the magnon-phonon detuning, driving a low-loss reflection zero across the real-frequency axis and producing two field-tunable RLs with near-vanishing reflection. A closed contour of the experimentally measured complex S11 around the reflection-zero singularity accumulates a -2pi phase winding. Independently, rotating the magnetic field tunes the magnon-phonon coupling strength, driving the intrinsic magnon-phonon eigenmode spectrum across an exceptional point, identified by the exchange between real-part and imaginary-part eigenvalue splitting. A unified one-port input-output model connects the measured complex S11 response to the field-driven dynamics of the reflection zeros and the angle-tuned intrinsic magnon-phonon eigenmodes. These results establish a magnetically programmable non-Hermitian magnon-phonon platform for integrated wave control and compact vector magnetic sensing.

title: MFlowAudio: Efficient Text-to-Audio Synthesis via Mamba-based Stateful Flow Matching
abstract: Recent advancements in audio generation have been largely driven by Transformer-based diffusion models. However, these models suffer from quadratic complexity of self-attention, severely bottlenecking the long-form audio synthesis. To overcome this limitation, we propose MFlowAudio, a novel latent audio generation framework that synergizes the continuous-time dynamics of Flow Matching with a custom-designed TCMamba backbone. TCMamba uses an innovative dual-scan mechanism: a TimeMamba module to capture long-range causal dependencies with linear complexity, and a ChannelMamba module to model cross-channel correlations such as harmonic structures. Exploiting this structural foundation, we formulate the Stateful Flow Matching (SFM) paradigm. This framework inherently enables chunk-wise training and streaming generation, maintaining an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ caching complexity without incurring extra computational overhead. To enable fine-grained controllable synthesis, we devise a novel guidance mechanism that neutralizes vector field collisions precipitated by on-the-fly semantic transitions of prompts. Comprehensive empirical evaluations confirm that MFlowAudio yields generative fidelity on par with state-of-the-art baselines while establishing significant computational efficiency, achieving above $14.5$% acceleration in generation and facilitating perceptually seamless streaming synthesis with a constant latency of $1.8$ seconds. Demo: https://huggingface.co/spaces/mflowaudio/MFlowAudio

title: Existence and uniqueness of the dual solution for obstacle problems in the space BV
abstract: We consider the variational problem of minimizing the multiple integral $\int_Ωf(\nabla u) \, dx$ with a convex density $f$ being of linear growth among functions $u$: $Ω\to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = u_0$ on $\partialΩ$ and for which $u \ge Ψ$ holds throughout the domain $Ω$. We prove that the dual problem has a unique solution. This result is extended to the case of interior obstacle problems, where the validity of $u \ge Ψ$ is only required on a subset $E$ of $Ω$. Moreover, we discuss the vectorial setting, i.e. the case of functions $u$: $Ω\to \mathbb{R}^N$, $N > 1$, combined with the additional condition $u(Ω) \subset A$ for a closed convex set $A \subset \mathbb{R}^N$, again showing the existence and the uniqueness of the associated dual solution.

title: LLM Recommenders Produce Demographic Inequality Through Content Preferences
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into systems that rank and recommend online content. We examine how this shift can produce demographic inequality in whose voices are surfaced. Using 10,000 Twitter/X posts written by 1,000 survey respondents and linked to verified self-reported characteristics across nine demographic attributes, we conduct a controlled recommendation experiment across three LLM providers, six recommendation objectives, and five levels of contextual information. By varying whether models receive post text alone, platform metadata, or explicit author demographics, we isolate three pathways to unequal recommendation: preferences for demographically patterned content, reliance on unequal engagement signals, and direct use of disclosed identity. We find that demographic inequality emerges from text alone. Models consistently favour longer, more negative, and more opinionated posts, particularly those concerning news and social issues, producing systematic differences in the demographic composition of recommended authors. Platform metadata generally amplifies these inequalities, while explicitly disclosing authors' demographic characteristics produces little additional change. Recommendation objectives mainly affect the magnitude of these patterns: controversial framing intensifies both content and demographic skew, whereas popularity-oriented framing dampens it, although for some attributes - most notably age - the objective can also reverse which group is favoured. LLM-based recommenders can therefore reproduce demographic inequality by proxy, not through explicit demographic targeting, but through preferences for content and engagement signals already structured by social inequality.

title: Iterated Integrals as Lexical Fingerprints: Path Signature Embeddings for Lexical Similarity
abstract: While sentence embeddings are primarily designed for semantic generalization, their latent geometry implicitly encodes surface-level lexical properties, a relationship that remains poorly understood. Shallow pooling methods discard word order, while deep Transformer models obscure these lexical alignments behind computational complexity and uninterpretable spaces. We propose constructing sentence embeddings via the path signature of Word2Vec trajectories, leveraging the iterated integrals of rough path theory to create representations that explicitly capture sequential and lexical structure in a geometrically tractable manner. Through extensive ablations spanning Word2Vec dimensions, signature depths, and PCA compression, we correlate embedding distances against five lexical string metrics: Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler, word Jaccard, phoneme Levenshtein, and character TF-IDF. We reveal that while average pooling almost entirely fails to capture character-level edit distances, path signatures strongly align with them, with depth 2 signatures optimally balancing character and word-level sensitivities. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the critical lexical variance is concentrated in a highly compact PCA subspace, and unlike pooling, signatures structurally preserve and quantify word order. These findings establish path signatures not as semantic generalizers, but as rigorous mathematical lenses that explicitly encode discrete lexical structures and word order, offering an interpretable alternative to opaque deep learning for lexical tracking.

title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
abstract: Conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents often use GUS-style architectures with separate modules for intent recognition, dialogue management, and template-based response generation. While faithful to the underlying XAI methods, these pipelines are hard to adapt and often struggle with context-dependent follow-up questions. We present SimXAI, a lightweight LLM-centric conversational layer that replaces these modules with a single tool-calling LLM that bridges access to existing XAI resources. Rather than a standalone agent, SimXAI serves as a modular interface that enables conversational access to external XAI resources. We further introduce an evaluation suite for single- and multi-turn parsing, faithfulness, and contextualization. Across existing and new datasets, SimXAI achieves strong function-selection accuracy and high faithfulness while better handling context-dependent requests. In a user study replacing only the conversational layer of TalkToModel, a representative GUS-based agent, users completed tasks more accurately and in fewer turn. Overall, SimXAI improves GUS-based design while preserving faithfulness and improving conversational quality.

title: When the Simulator Fails, Not the Policy: Auditing Contact Artifacts in Simulated Robot Benchmarks
abstract: Simulation benchmarks score robot policies by success rate, and every failed episode counts against the policy. Many of these failures are the simulator's fault, not the policy's; we find the cause and fix it. Testing a vision language action model and a world action model in simulation, we find that the policy often places the object and the simulator then ejects it, and that the benchmark's own scripted demonstrations fail the same way. We present SimuGuard, an auditing plugin for LIBERO, RoboTwin, RoboCasa and RoboDojo. It leaves the evaluation unchanged. At every physics step, it records the state and flags an object that starts moving at a contact faster than the robot's contact or gravity account for. It replays a recorded episode bit for bit, and it reruns the episode with one simulation parameter changed. With it we trace these episodes on RoboTwin to the collision detection of the physics engine: for geometry one to two centimeters apart, the engine reports a penetration of about two centimeters, and the solver throws the object out at several meters per second. The cause is one constant: the distance algorithm discards triangles below a fixed area threshold, which valid triangles fall below at the centimeter scale. With that constant changed and nothing else, episodes with an artifact fall from 12 in 100 to none, and the success rate on five container tasks rises from 89% to 98%. Success rates in simulation thus count failures that the simulator causes. Benchmarks on PhysX 5.3.1 or earlier should rerun in a repaired engine. Where the engine cannot change, they should report the success rate together with the range it spans when every flagged episode fails or passes: 75.8% to 98.5% around a reported 83.1% for LingBot-VA.

title: Channel dichotomies
abstract: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

title: Batch Universal Prediction via Conditional Additive Smoothing
abstract: Modern language models motivate renewed interest in universal prediction problems in which a predictor can exploit previously observed data before predicting a fresh sequence. We study an idealized version of this setting by introducing \emph{batch regret}: a conditional analogue of classical average regret in which a predictor observes a batch of $n$ training sequences and is then evaluated on an independent test sequence generated by the same unknown source. Additive smoothing estimators, which add a bias to the observed token frequencies before predicting the next token, played a fundamental role as a simple prediction strategy with almost-optimal average regret for memoryless and Markov sources. Their equivalent under batch regret are the conditional additive smoothing estimators, which estimate the conditional distribution of the test sequence given the training batch. In this work, we study their asymptotical batch regret for binary memoryless and first-order Markov sources. For binary memoryless sources, we show how the optimal bias of the estimator, and consequently the corresponding batch regret, change as a function of the training batch size $n$, by extending the Poisson-based analysis of Krichevsky. For binary Markov sources with positive transitions, we characterize the leading coefficient of batch regret and its dependence on whether the initial law is known, free, or stationary. Finally, we introduce a Rényi analogue of batch regret and identify the corresponding optimal predictors as conditional $α$-NML estimators, thereby giving an operational interpretation to a conditional version of Sibson's $α$-mutual information.

title: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information
abstract: The problem of transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel with causal state information is addressed. The state comprises three independent components: a common component, which is revealed to both en- coders, and two private components, each of which is revealed to a different encoder. The data are to be recovered with arbitrarily-small probability of error, and the state sequence with arbitrarily-small symbol-error rate. Under the assumption that the capacity region in the absence of a state recon- struction constraint is nonempty, the capacity region is derived and is shown to be achievable using a Block-Markov coding scheme employing binning and superposition coding.

title: Layered Reproducibility for High-Performance Computing Applications: The Feel++ and Ktirio Urban Buildings Case Study
abstract: The High-Performance Computing (HPC) community struggles with reproducibility due to complex software stacks, heterogeneous hardware, and expensive validation cycles. This contribution presents a layered reproducibility strategy in which Feel++ provides a traceable software supply chain and Ktirio Urban Buildings (KUB) builds on it to manage versioned urban-building data, executable simulations, and checksum-verifiable result artifacts. Feel++ treats continuous integration (CI) plans, CMake presets, packaging manifests, public software metadata, operations commands, containers, software bill of materials (SBOM)/provenance metadata, and Feel++ Benchmarking reports for Feel++ and KUB cases as repositoryowned artifacts. KUB applies this foundation to City Energy Model Database (CEMDB) datasets, manifests, Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) packaging, and verifiable outputs for computationally expensive simulations. The case study shifts reproducibility from late manual packaging to an artifact chain linking source commits, packages, containers, benchmark configurations, dataset versions, provenance records, and generated results.

title: Loose Inductive Set Theories
abstract: We prove that KP, with Full Set Induction, is neither solid nor tight. More generally, every consistent theory obtained from KPC by adding a quantifier bounded set of sentences has a model with a parameter-free definable class surjection from its natural numbers onto its universe. Using such enumerations to define generic extensions by relative interpretations, we show that theories with the stable definable ground property are not tight. Ground definability over MOST and continuum coding over ZFC^{Π_3} yield applications to weak inductive set theories with large cardinals and forcing axioms. Finally, solidity for quantifier bounded extensions of MOST with Full Set Induction implies a Ground Axiom formulated using a fixed finite level of genericity; under the same solidity hypothesis, the corresponding extension of full ZFC proves the ordinary Ground Axiom.

title: Stuck on Red? Understanding GitHub Actions Failing Streaks
abstract: GitHub Actions is the de facto CI/CD service for GitHub repositories. Its workflows should not fail when they are not expected to, nor keep on failing too long. We empirically study failing streaks, i.e., uninterrupted series of failing runs of a workflow, in 30.9M+ runs of 154K+ workflows of 43K+ GitHub repositories over 238 days. We study how failing streaks begin and end, and what happens during them, based on the trigger and the commit of each run. We also classify all workflows by their purposes, such as building, testing or deploying, and we inspect the logs of a small sample of failing streaks. Failing runs mostly come in streaks: three quarters of them follow another failing run, and half of the workflows with at least three runs have at least one failing streak. Workflows serving multiple purposes have failing streaks more often, even at the same size. Most failing streaks end within hours, but the one in five that last more than a day account for the lion's share of the time that workflows spend failing. A third of the failing streaks start, and two in five end, without any change to the repository. In a sample of 100 failing streaks, those that end this way most often fail because of network issues or an external service. These findings suggest that maintainers should not assume that a failure comes from the last commit. GitHub and tool builders could flag failures that occur without any change to the repository, and alert the active maintainers when a workflow stays failing for more than a day.

title: Generative sampling with physics-informed kernels
abstract: We construct a generative network for Monte-Carlo sampling in lattice field theories and beyond, for which the layerwise propagation is computed and optimised independently on each layer. The architecture uses physics-informed renormalisation group flows that provide access to the layerwise propagation step from one layer to the next in terms of a simple first order partial differential equation for the respective renormalisation group kernel through a given layer. Thus, it transforms the generative task into that of solving once the set of independent and linear differential equations for the kernels of the transformation. As these equations are analytically known, the kernels can be refined iteratively. This allows us to structurally tackle out-of-domain problems generally encountered in generative models and opens the path to further optimisation. We illustrate the practical feasibility of the architecture within simulations in scalar field theories.

title: Learning to Interact and Direct: Co-Evolving Video Director Agents
abstract: Video director agents orchestrate multistage production to realize users' creative visions. Emerging research on their self-evolution advances screenplay planning effectively. However, the mutual reinforcement between directing and user interaction remains largely overlooked. Improved interaction clarifies user intent and informs workflow refinement, while more reliable execution shifts collaboration from troubleshooting to creative decisions. To this end, we introduce LIT (Learning to Interact and DirecT), a framework comprises a director agent, a simulated user, and a meta engineer. Simulated user assigns creative tasks to probe the director's weaknesses, while the meta engineer uses the task traces to revise the director's interaction and production strategy. Although this approach can address discovered interaction and production issues, it still relies on passive attribution by the meta agent. This limits its ability to adapt to broader user interaction patterns and production techniques. To solve this problem, we equip LIT with a co-evolution paradigm. The meta agent proactively learns external knowledge, thereby improving its ability to discover problems and propose solutions. The meta agent, simulated user, and director together form an evolutionary closed loop, collaboratively enhances the system's directing and interaction capabilities. Across the Test and OOD Test splits, LIT improves production and Interaction scores by 19.1% and 32.0%, respectively, relative to the initial pipeline. Controlled ablations reveal the correlation between improvements in production and interaction, where the co-evolution mechanism further encourage directing skill and interaction mode exploration.

title: AI evaluators favor job applications written by certain AI models, independent of candidate quality
abstract: Job applicants increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to write cover letters, while employers deploy LLMs to screen them. In this all-AI setting, we ask whether the \emph{choice of model} affects hiring outcomes independently of candidate qualifications. We introduce a multi-model auditing framework pairing eleven LLM writer agents with nine API-hosted evaluator agents across ten job descriptions and fifty candidates per job. Four findings emerge. First, we identify a generative preference hierarchy: a consistent global ranking of writer models by evaluator acceptance, in which locally hosted models are systematically disadvantaged regardless of their license, compounded by self-preference bias where evaluators favour their own outputs. Second, evaluator models differ substantially in how much bias they introduce based on applicants' tool choice, offering actionable guidance for fairer screening design. Third, this hierarchy has measurable competitive consequences: in the most adverse pairing, approximately two (1.8) out of twenty-five qualified candidates are filtered out purely due to model mismatch. Fourth, a common mechanism explains the patterns above: writer preference and self-preference trace to a combination of how much each writer leans on specific stylistic cues and how strongly evaluators, often unanimously, reward or penalise those same cues. A further check finds little evidence that an unmeasured "writer fingerprint" remains once these same features are accounted for. We discuss implications for algorithmic fairness in employment, regulation of AI-assisted screening, and the design of auditing frameworks that can be reapplied as the model landscape evolves.

title: The twistor construction of toric gravitational instantons
abstract: We give an explicit construction of all ALF and ALE toric gravitational instantons in terms of certain rational matrix functions of one complex variable on the Riemann sphere; these provide patching matrices for their corresponding twistor holomorphic vector bundles. The reconstruction of the instantons arises from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert splitting problem and we show how this can be solved via linear algebra, resembling but not equivalent to the Belinski--Zakharov ansatz. This construction gives a complete classification together with an explicit form for all toric gravitational instantons up to the resolutions of conical and orbifold singularities. We illustrate the formalism by computer--assisted numerical construction of two new ALF (but not AF) gravitational instantons with five nodes.

title: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots
abstract: LLM-based robotic agent systems can generate programs for robot control, yet their generalization to new tasks often depends on elaborate scaffolding. Expanding their skill repertoires alone offers limited guidance on how to assess new capabilities or identify what remains beyond their reach. We introduce META-Robot, a framework that couples self cognition with capability scaling by expanding the criteria through which an agent evaluates and develops its skills. At its core, action-level predicates make execution outcomes explicit and available for LLM reasoning. The agent uses these assessments to identify its own limitations, extend relevant evaluation criteria, and guide the structured expansion of its skills. Proprioceptive feedback further grounds this process in the robot's physical state, enriching the evidence available for self-cognition. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate stronger overall task performance, generalization to new tasks, continued expansion of skills and evaluation criteria, and effective use of non-visual proprioceptive signals.

title: A four-dimensional residue calculus for quaternionic slice regular functions
abstract: We develop a 4-dimensional residue calculus for quaternionic slice semiregular functions. Its local singularities are isolated real poles and 2-dimensional spheres.
